items.title: Weakness Localization Is Not Enough: State-Aware Recursive Knowledge Improvement for Large Language Models

items.summary: JevRec introduces a linguistic encoding and Jev-like decision modeling approach for LLM-based generative recommendation systems. It addresses the issue of uniform semantic identifier lengths for items with varying interaction frequencies.

items.title: Text Generation in Low-Resource Languages Using Human-Curated Vocabularies

items.title: PRISM-AMC: Replay-Free Continual Learning for Automatic Modulation Classification
items.summary: This research proposes PRISM-AMC, a replay-free continual learning approach for Automatic Modulation Classification (AMC), addressing challenges in adapting to new modulation classes without access to past training data.

items.title: Learning When to Think Aloud in Latent Reasoning
items.summary: This research explores a method for 'Learning When to Think Aloud' in latent reasoning, aiming to improve the precision of Chain-of-Thought approaches for tasks like mathematical reasoning by selectively externalizing intermediate steps.

items.title: Short-Term Forecasting of Heterogeneous Wind Power Fleets: Global Temporal Fusion Transformer Leveraging Static Covariates
items.summary: This study investigates short-term forecasting for heterogeneous wind power fleets using a global Temporal Fusion Transformer that leverages static covariates, aiming to improve grid stability and electricity trading.

items.title: Neural Stochastic Forecasting for Lateral Molecular Diffusion Simulations
items.summary: This research introduces a neural stochastic (NS) model for forecasting lateral molecular diffusion, offering a computationally efficient method for predicting long-time diffusion of membrane proteins compared to traditional simulations.

items.title: Selective Prediction Intervals: Jointly Learning to Predict, Bound, and Abstain
items.summary: This paper proposes 'Selective Prediction Intervals,' a deep learning method that jointly learns to provide point estimates, bound risks with intervals, and offer an option to abstain for high-stakes regression decisions.

items.title: FaCoDiff: Factor-Correlated Diffusion for Multivariate Probabilistic Forecasting
items.summary: This research introduces Factor-Correlated Diffusion (FaCoDiff), a novel approach for multivariate probabilistic forecasting that models cross-variable dependence while managing marginal noise scales and covariance costs.

items.title: Cross-Asset Knowledge Transfer for Early Fault Detection of Data-Scarce Assets Without Target Fault Data
items.summary: This paper addresses early fault detection in data-scarce industrial assets by investigating cross-asset knowledge transfer methods, aiming to improve reliability management even without target fault data.

items.title: Rubric Curriculum RL: Exploiting the Generation-Verification Gap in Non-Verifiable Domains
items.summary: This research proposes 'Rubric Curriculum RL,' a method to exploit the generation-verification gap in non-verifiable domains, extending the gains of reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards to open-ended tasks.

items.title: DS@GT ARC at CheckThat! 2026: A Verdict-Anchored Pipeline for Generating Fact-Checking Articles
items.summary: This paper details a 'Verdict-Anchored Pipeline' for generating fact-checking articles, developed by the DS@GT ARC team for CLEF 2026 CheckThat! Lab Task 3, to automate the production of fact-checking content.

items.title: CCDWIKI: Decoupling Case Formulation from Response Generation in Longitudinal CBT Dialogue
items.summary: This research introduces CCDWIKI, a method for decoupling case formulation from response generation in longitudinal Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT) dialogue systems.

items.title: Human-like cross-language generalisation in deep neural speaker embeddings and its acoustic foundations
items.summary: This study investigates human-like cross-language generalization in deep neural speaker embeddings and its underlying acoustic foundations, exploring how these embeddings perform across different languages.

items.title: Same Origin, Different Verdicts: Text Production Conditions Confound Machine-Generated Text Detection in Russian
items.summary: This research examines how text production conditions can confound the automated detection of machine-generated text, specifically in Russian, highlighting that origin is a property of the process, not just the text itself.

items.title: When to Ask, When to Answer: Strategic Clarification for Ambiguous Reference Resolution in Dialogue
items.summary: This research examines how large language models (LLMs) tend to answer prematurely in dialogue and proposes strategic clarification methods for ambiguous reference resolution.

items.title: Rewrite, Then Veto: Rewriter-Agnostic Edit Gating for LLM-Based Post-OCR Correction
items.summary: This paper proposes EditVeto, a method using a veto gate after an LLM rewrite to correct noisy OCR transcripts without altering already correct text.

items.title: Contextual Pictograms for Repairing Multilingual ASR Errors
items.summary: This work describes an interface that uses alternative transcripts, replay, and contextual pictograms to help users recognize and repair errors in multilingual ASR outputs.

items.title: Matching the Training-Time Weight Rule in Inference-Time Expert Deactivation
items.summary: This paper compares different implementations of expert deactivation at inference time, such as removal and freezing, and their effects on token routing and expert weights in models.

items.title: When Does Better Confidence Improve a Knowledge-Graph Audit?
items.summary: This study investigates how confidence estimates guide human review in LLM-built knowledge graphs, analyzing factors like repairability and selection headroom that affect audit improvement.

items.title: Selective, Risk-Controlled Emotion Forecasting in Conversation: From a Persistence Barrier to Departure Detection with Conformal Guarantees
items.summary: This research proposes a learnable and deployable reformulation for forecasting emotion in conversation, moving from predicting the next emotional state to detecting emotional departure with guarantees.

items.title: Familiar letters, not related languages, let unseen languages into a shared space of meaning
items.summary: This study finds that familiar letter systems, rather than related languages, are key for AI models to incorporate unseen languages into a shared semantic space.

items.title: When Every Choice Is Correct: A Causal Study of Numerical Preference in Language Models
items.summary: This causal study investigates numerical preference in language models when all choices are valid, analyzing how preferences are processed across layers and tokens.

items.title: Adapting Qwen3 to Tajik from 0.6B to 8B: Lower Text Loss Did Not Mean Better Understanding
items.summary: This research investigates adapting the Qwen3 model to Tajik using LoRA adapters, finding that while text loss decreased, reading comprehension did not improve significantly.

items.title: Mass Producing Training Data with Surprising Side Effects
items.summary: This study examines how the mass production of training data can lead to surprising and unintended side effects on language model behavior, including misalignment and persona induction, making generalization challenging to understand.

items.title: Replicability, Reproducibility, and Robustness in Political and Social Science Research with Large Language Models
items.summary: This chapter addresses the challenges of replicability, reproducibility, and robustness in political and social science research that uses large language models, highlighting issues stemming from probabilistic and variable LLM outputs.

items.title: ALTO: African and Levantine Tech-Facilitated Gender-Based Violence Corpus
items.summary: This paper introduces ALTO, a new corpus for detecting Tech-Facilitated Gender-Based Violence (TFGBV) in African and Levantine languages, aiming to address the data imbalance in current models for harm detection.

items.title: Persona Perspectives: Adopting Viewpoints Reorganizes Representations in LLMs
items.summary: This paper investigates how adopting different "personas" reorganizes internal representations in Large Language Models (LLMs), challenging assumptions of consistent feature representation across contexts.

items.title: Visual Forensic Detection of Fabricated Bangla News Photocards using Deep Learning
items.summary: This research applies deep learning for visual forensic detection of fabricated Bangla news photocards, addressing localized misinformation spread through single-image news summaries.

items.title: mmHand: Toward Pixel-Level-Accuracy Hand Localization Using a Single Commodity mmWave Device
items.summary: This paper presents mmHand, a method for achieving pixel-level-accuracy hand localization using a single commodity mmWave device, addressing limitations in existing hand localization technologies.

items.title: PEEK: One-Step-Look-Ahead Exposure Bias Correction for Diffusion Sampling
items.summary: This paper introduces PEEK, a one-step-look-ahead exposure bias correction method designed to improve the sampling process in diffusion image generators by addressing the train-test gap.

items.title: Augmentation with Reinforcement Transformation for Low-textured Scientific Sketch Image Retrieval
items.summary: This research proposes an augmentation method using reinforcement transformation to improve image retrieval for challenging low-textured scientific sketch images in various applications.

items.title: PointNDF: Cascaded Neural Displacement Fields for Point Cloud Denoising
items.summary: This paper introduces PointNDF, a method utilizing cascaded neural displacement fields for point cloud denoising, aiming to recover clean 3D geometry while preserving fine surface details.

items.title: SO(3)-Equivariant Learning on CAD Boundary Representations
items.summary: This research explores SO(3)-Equivariant Learning for CAD Boundary Representations (B-reps) to improve robustness to part pose, addressing limitations of existing B-rep networks under rotation.

items.title: From Tokens to Trajectories: Parameter-Efficient Continuous Adaptation of Unified Multimodal Models
items.summary: This paper introduces FlowShift, a parameter-efficient method for continuous adaptation of Unified Multimodal Models (UMMs), aiming to overcome the quantization bottleneck that degrades fine visual details.

items.title: Discarded or Unreachable? Diagnosing and Repairing Spatial Relation Failure in Vision--Language Similarity
items.summary: This research diagnoses spatial relation failures in vision-language models, identifying whether the issue lies in the accessibility of relations or their discard during pooling, and suggests different repair strategies.

items.title: Role-based Effectiveness of an Epistemic Uncertainty Estimate in Training Models for Semantic Segmentation of 3D LiDAR Point Clouds
items.summary: This paper investigates the effectiveness of epistemic uncertainty estimates in training models for semantic segmentation of 3D LiDAR point clouds, addressing challenges due to sparsity and noise in data.

items.title: Multimodal Fusion Methods for Whole-Slide Images and Clinical Data in Inflammatory Bowel Disease
items.summary: This paper presents a modular framework for comparing multimodal AI fusion methods for whole-slide images and clinical data in computational pathology, specifically for Inflammatory Bowel Disease.

items.title: CAPTOR: text-encoder-free grounding by counting caption co-occurrence over the visual words of a frozen encoder
items.summary: CAPTOR is a new method for text-encoder-free grounding of text queries in images by counting caption co-occurrence over the visual words of a frozen encoder, addressing a limitation in vision-language models.

items.title: Spatio-Temporal Multi-Order Interaction for Video Recognition
items.summary: This paper proposes a new method for Spatio-Temporal Multi-Order Interaction for video recognition, aiming to reduce computational overhead caused by explicit cross-channel aggregation projections.

items.title: ARIDA - Active railway infrastructure dataset annotation using neural network predictions
items.summary: ARIDA is an Active Railway Infrastructure Dataset Annotation framework that uses neural network predictions to assist in creating large image datasets for railway perception, particularly for complex geometries.

items.title: Toward an Optimal Configuration for Tree Species Classification from Bark Images: A Leakage-Safe Ablation Study
items.summary: This study conducts a leakage-safe ablation study to determine optimal configurations for deep-learning approaches in automatically classifying tree species from bark images.

items.title: TRUST-Stereo: Teacher-Assisted Robust Uncertainty-Guided Search and Transfer for Fast Stereo Matching
items.summary: TRUST-Stereo proposes a Teacher-Assisted Robust Uncertainty-Guided Search and Transfer method to improve fast stereo matching by addressing sensitivity to errors in propagated disparity.

items.title: Anchored Slice Propagation with Boundary Transport for 3D CT Segmentation from Three Orthogonal Annotated Slices
items.summary: This research presents Anchored Slice Propagation with Boundary Transport, a new method for 3D CT segmentation that uses three orthogonal annotated slices to improve mask propagation reliability.

items.title: GeoDIVE: Geospatial Descent Informed by Value Estimation
items.summary: GeoDIVE is a new system designed for geospatial descent informed by value estimation, used to efficiently find specific objects and patterns in large regions for applications like agriculture and disaster response.

items.title: Mitigating Spurious Invariance in Contrastive Learning: A Probabilistic Self-Supervised Learning Framework for Medical Image Analysis
items.summary: This paper introduces a probabilistic self-supervised learning framework to mitigate spurious invariance in contrastive learning, aiming to improve medical image analysis without extensive manual annotation.

items.title: Learning Hierarchical Patch Splitting Policies for Faster Vision Transformers
items.summary: This research focuses on learning hierarchical patch splitting policies to make Vision Transformers faster by adaptively adjusting patch sizes based on image content, reducing token sequence length.

items.title: Decompose the Distillation: Interpretable Single-Pass Guidance for Diffusion Models
items.summary: This paper introduces Interpretable Single-Pass Guidance for diffusion models, a method that decomposes distillation to provide a more flexible and efficient guidance rule for conditional image generation.

items.title: ReTailor: A Residual Feature Tailoring Framework for Real-Time Cross-Sensor Pansharpening Adaptation
items.summary: This paper presents ReTailor, a framework for adapting pansharpening models to new sensors in real-time without extensive retraining or target-sensor specific data.

items.title: Generative AI for urban planning: synthesizing land-use maps with satellite imagery via DualControlNet
items.summary: This paper explores using generative AI with DualControlNet to synthesize new land-use maps from satellite imagery for urban planning, moving beyond predictive models.

items.title: Feature Puzzles: Single-Image Supervision for Multi-View 3D-Aware Segmentation
items.summary: This paper proposes 'Feature Puzzles,' a method for achieving multi-view 3D-aware segmentation using only single-image supervision, reducing the need for expensive video or multi-view data.

items.title: DecoupAttn: Decoupled Sparse Attention for Training-Free Acceleration of Video Diffusion
items.summary: This paper proposes DecoupAttn, a decoupled sparse attention mechanism that provides training-free acceleration for video diffusion transformers by optimizing key block computations.

items.title: Modality-Aware Expert Pruning for MoE-Based Multimodal Large Language Models
items.summary: This paper introduces modality-aware expert pruning for Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) based multimodal large language models to significantly reduce their memory footprint.

items.title: CLEAR: Color-Texture Latent Alignment for Single Image Reflection Removal
items.summary: This paper presents CLEAR, a method for single image reflection removal that uses color-texture latent alignment to recover transmitted scenes from photographs captured through glass.

items.title: PathoS2VD: From 2D Histopathology to Pseudo Z-Stack Representations
items.summary: This paper introduces PathoS2VD, a method that generates pseudo Z-stack representations from 2D histopathology images, addressing the inherent 3D morphology of biological tissues.

items.title: Clips2Story: Training-Free Video Storyboarding and Editing Using Multimodal Retrieval-Embedded Generation
items.summary: This paper proposes Clips2Story, a training-free method for video storyboarding and editing that uses multimodal retrieval-embedded generation to organize fragmented footage into coherent narratives.

items.title: FedIA: Instance-Aware Cross-Modal Representations for Federated Prompt Learning
items.summary: This paper introduces FedIA, a method that uses instance-aware cross-modal representations for federated prompt learning, enabling efficient adaptation of vision-language models across decentralized clients.

items.title: ChanSFormer: A Channel Agnostic Vision Transformer for Multi-Channel Cell Painting Images
items.summary: This paper presents ChanSFormer, a channel-agnostic vision transformer designed for multi-channel cell painting images and other heterogeneous multi-channel imaging data in scientific pipelines.

items.title: METRIC-GS: Selective Metric-Scale Estimation for 3D Gaussian Splatting
items.summary: This paper introduces METRIC-GS, a method for selective metric-scale estimation in 3D Gaussian Splatting reconstructions, allowing for accurate measurements and AR content placement.

items.title: USI-Brain: Enhancing Underwater Spatial Intelligence via Spatial Data-Driven Vision-Language Modeling
items.summary: This paper proposes USI-Brain, a framework that enhances underwater spatial intelligence by leveraging spatial data-driven vision-language modeling to overcome visual challenges in underwater environments.

items.title: UniRestorer++: Scalable Universal Image Restoration with Multi-Granularity Degradation Modeling
items.summary: This paper introduces UniRestorer++, a method for scalable universal image restoration that handles diverse degradations within a single model through multi-granularity degradation modeling.

items.title: RI-Prune: Relation and Information Aware Visual Token Pruning for Multi-Image Vision-Language Models
items.summary: This paper introduces RI-Prune, a relation and information-aware visual token pruning method for multi-image vision-language models to improve efficiency by managing the increased visual token budget.

items.title: SVGFaith: A Two-Layer Meta-Evaluation of Faithfulness Metrics for Text-to-SVG Generation
items.summary: Text-to-SVG systems are commonly evaluated by applying raster-image metrics to rasterised outputs, yet whether these scores capture fine-grained prompt faithfulness remains unclear. We introduce SVGFaith, a two-layer meta-evaluation framework in which the more faithful candidate of each pair is determined by construction or by human judgment. SVGFaith-Diagnostic contains 1,842 controlled contrastive pairs across eight capability axes, split evenly between two directions: two renderings compared against one prompt, and two descriptions compared against one rendering. SVGFaith-Arena contains 1,327 human-annotated comparisons of real generator outputs. On SVGFaith-Diagnostic, CLIP and three other image--text embedding metrics reach at least 0.789 pairwise accuracy on object identity but at most 0.672 on spatial relations and attribute binding, where chance is 0.5. We further introduce SVGFaith-Score, an interpretable pointwise metric. A domain-tuned decomposer turns each prompt into a dependency graph of atomic visual requirements, a visual question answering model scores whether each requirement is satisfied, and a requirement's score is discounted when its prerequisites score low. In addition to the overall score, the per-requirement scores show which requirements are judged unsatisfied and which inherit discounts from their prerequisites. SVGFaith-Score significantly outperforms all nine baselines, including a Qwen3.5-122B-A10B judge, on Arena and in both Diagnostic directions. Code and data: https://github.com/Yukinonooo/SVGFaith.

items.title: Touch\'{e}World tech report : Towards Online Unified Camera--Hand Exploration in Generative Worlds
items.summary: Recent video world models allow users to explore generated environments through camera navigation. Continuous hand motion provides a fine-grained action channel for interacting with the people and objects encountered during exploration. We present Touch\'{e}World, a framework that integrates gesture-driven interaction into a camera-controlled video world model. Given an initial image and a scene-description prompt, the model generates video conditioned on temporally aligned camera and hand controls. We construct joint camera--hand training data from heterogeneous egocentric videos through annotation completion, consistency-based filtering, and temporal alignment. Building on a pretrained camera-controlled world model, we combine spatial hand-skeleton conditioning with numerical hand-motion features through parameter-efficient adaptation. Causal adaptation and few-step distillation support chunk-level online generation, allowing users to update their controls based on generated visual feedback. We further introduce Touch\'{e}Bench to evaluate hand-motion following, camera--hand coordination, online interaction, and object response. Together, these components establish a framework for studying continuous exploration and hand-driven interaction within generative worlds.

items.title: RouTex: Multi-reference 3D Texture Generation by Reprogramming Rotary Position Encoding
items.summary: While single-image 3D texture generation has advanced significantly, conditioning texture synthesis on multi-view reference images remains largely under-explored, despite its necessity for resolving surface ambiguity in unobserved regions. In this paper, we propose RouTex, a novel multi-reference 3D texture generation framework based on in-context Diffusion Transformers (DiT). Our key insight is that native 3D Rotary Position Encoding (RoPE) inherently possesses spatial addressing capabilities. We introduce Positional Routing (PR) to reprogram 3D RoPE along spatial and semantic dimensions, establishing explicit reference-to-view correspondence without introducing additional parameters. To execute this routing efficiently, Dual-Granularity Attention (DGA) combines per-view local attention for fine texture fidelity with global joint attention over deduplicated references for cross-view consistency. Extensive experiments demonstrate that RouTex achieves new state-of-the-art performance in multi-reference 3D texture generation.

items.title: Jev with Foresight: Safe Language-Guided Autonomous Driving via a Language World Model
items.summary: Large language models understand passengers' driving commands, but as driving agents they reason in generated text for seconds and must infer each action's consequences implicitly from the scene. We present Jev-AD, which pairs Jev, a typed decision model that answers predefined questions with probabilities, not generated text, with a language world model that predicts for every candidate action how nearby vehicles move over the next two seconds. Code turns these predictions into foreseen consequences, which Jev compares instead of inferring them from coordinates. In simulated highway merging (500 car-episodes), this foresight lowers the same decision model's collision rate from 26.0% to 2.4% at 0.25 seconds per decision, and Jev-AD achieves the passenger's intent in 93% of free-form command trials. In 500 replayed real-world NGSIM episodes, foresight lowers the collision rate from 48.2% to 2.8%, and the world model, learned from this traffic, foresees 93% of dangerous actions. Project page: https://ys-qu.github.io/jev-ad-website.

items.title: Ctrl-F: Force as an Interface for Humanoid Loco-Manipulation
items.summary: Humanoid motion tracking has scaled to general policies that reproduce diverse human motion, but the resulting behavior is in free-space: the tracker knows where the body should be, not how it should interact with the environment. Other work makes the object part of the objective, yet abstracts that interaction to contact or geometry, which leaves the demanding cases under-explored. We argue that force is a natural command channel between motion imitation and object interaction, one that specifies not just where to make contact but how hard. We present Ctrl-F, a hierarchical motion-force framework that augments motion tracking with an explicit force command, a 3-D force at each designated contact body such as a hand or a foot. The hierarchical framework comprises: (1) A unified motion-force controller tracks the reference motion while applying the commanded force to the world. (2) A high-level force planner that issues a force command online based on object state and proprioception observations. In simulation and on hardware, Ctrl-F completes loco-manipulation that demands large, sustained interaction force and adjusts its command online as the load changes, both out of reach of a force-blind tracker. On hardware, Ctrl-F demonstrates hand-based dragging, pushing, and lifting, as well as foot-based kicking, successfully manipulating boxes weighing up to 20kg in pushing and kicking tasks where the force-blind baseline fails, while adapting online to additional loads introduced mid-task.

items.title: MESA: An Evaluation Framework for Compositional, Semantic, and Spatial Generalization in Robotics
items.summary: Despite growing interest in foundation models for robotic manipulation, systematic evaluation of their capabilities remains elusive. Existing benchmarks are either narrow and saturated, offering little signal on SOTA methods, broadly scoped, providing diversity at the cost of controlled experimentation, or require training on large, messy open-source datasets. We introduce MESA, an evaluation framework designed for precise, reproducible measurement of language-conditioned policy generalization. MESA provides five evaluation suites that isolate in-distribution performance and four distinct axes of generalization: spatial configuration, object instance, object category, and subtask composition, enabling researchers to diagnose where and why policies fail, not just whether they fail. To populate these suites at scale, we develop MESA-Gen, a pipeline for task and demonstration generation built by improving MimicGen. We instantiate the framework on two platforms and release both: the single-arm MESA suite, and BiMESA, the first large-scale benchmark for bimanual generalization. We evaluate seven baseline methods spanning diffusion policies, VLM-based approaches, and pretrained VLAs, finding that the strongest model achieves only 52% on MESA and 49% on BiMESA, providing meaningful signal while leaving ample room for progress. MESA rankings are broadly consistent with RoboArena scores, suggesting that MESA captures method-level differences relevant beyond simulation. Project website: https://pairlab.github.io/MESA.

items.title: Contact-Implicit Whole-Body Trajectory Optimization for Dynamic Humanoid Locomotion on Parameterizable Uneven Terrain
items.summary: This letter presents a trajectory planner for humanoid robots to perform dynamic motions on complex, parameterizable terrains using a contact-implicit whole-body optimization framework. The planner generates feasible movements without predefined contact sequences, considering the robot's full dynamics and kinematics. To plan bipedal locomotion on steps, ramps, and other terrains, we propose a mathematical model to approximate ground geometry with a smooth surface. The rigid interaction between the robot and the ground is modeled via novel contact constraints, extending the domain of applicability from flat and horizontal surfaces to any arbitrary smooth surface. Effectiveness is demonstrated using nonlinear programming to plan motions on various terrain topologies. We also explore dynamic trajectory generation by embedding high-level requirements in the cost function and the initial guess. Preliminary feasibility tests were conducted over non-coplanar terrains, both in simulation and on the real robot ErgoCub.

items.title: Correct Robots Before They Make Mistakes: Proactive Human-in-the-Loop Intervention via Preference Learning
items.summary: This paper presents Proactive Human-in-the-Loop (PHIL), a framework for proactive policy correction and preference-based post-training. PHIL enables operators to preview policy-predicted future motion and intervene before anticipated undesirable actions. During takeover, PHIL continues querying the policy and displaying its predicted trajectories in the physical workspace through an extended reality (XR) interface. PHIL pairs rejected policy predictions with corrective action chunks subsequently executed from the same physical state over the same horizon, and preference-based post-training encourages the policy to favor these corrections. This paper evaluates PHIL on four real-world manipulation tasks using a diffusion policy and a pretrained vision-language-action policy. With five correction episodes per condition, PHIL increases mean success rates across the evaluated tasks and demonstration budgets from 44.0% to 70.3% for the diffusion policy and from 57.8% to 76.9% for X-VLA, compared with HG-DAgger. Separately, policies trained with proactive corrections show fewer unnecessary recovery behaviors in successful episodes. Project page: https://intuitive-robots.github.io/PHIL-page/.

items.title: OdorSpaces: Visual-Olfactory Embodied Navigation in 3D Environments
items.summary: Olfaction provides critical information about airborne chemical cues, yet it remains largely underexplored in embodied AI, with limited prior machine olfaction work focusing primarily on semantic odor perception. We introduce OdorSpaces, a physics-based simulation platform and benchmark for visual-olfactory embodied navigation. OdorSpaces augments Habitat-Sim with 3D odor transport and dispersion simulated by Fire Dynamics Simulator (FDS), enabling agents to navigate photorealistic indoor environments using both visual and olfactory observations. The benchmark includes two representative source-seeking scenarios: invisible gas-leak localization and early-stage fire localization. We develop an initial multimodal reinforcement learning policy that integrates visual observations and olfactory measurements over time. Experiments show that the policy outperforms a diverse set of baselines, establishing a strong reference for future research on visual-olfactory embodied navigation.

items.title: GRASP: Gradient-Guided Sampling for Contact-Rich Physics-Based Motion Retargeting
items.summary: We study physics-based retargeting of human demonstrations for robot learning: finding robot controls that reproduce reference motions under contact dynamics. We propose GRASP (Gradient Recovery from Archived Samples for Proposals), which combines sampling-based exploration with gradient-guided refinement without requiring a differentiable simulator. GRASP-TO extends tempered sequential Monte Carlo by fitting local quadratic cost models to archived rollouts and using their gradients to guide Markov chain Monte Carlo rejuvenation. Metropolis-Hastings correction preserves the target distribution for each fixed proposal kernel, and a population analysis connects the recovered gradients to Gaussian smoothing. GRASP-MPC scales this optimizer to long demonstrations through warm-started receding-horizon planning. Experiments on dexterous hands and humanoids show accurate retargeting with a shared tracking objective and no task-specific contact rewards, including 92.8% success on 1352 bimanual OakInk2 demonstrations. The refined references improve PPO tracking in pen spinning and humanoid-object interaction. We also demonstrate dexterous manipulation and whole-body humanoid motion on real hardware.

items.title: Closed-Loop Adaptive Sampling on a Generative Ocean Model
items.summary: Adaptive sampling can substantially improve the value of sparse ocean observations by directing mobile robots toward measurements that are most informative for an evolving environment. Recent learned generative ocean models can produce high-resolution forecasts and ensembles at substantially lower computational cost than traditional numerical models, creating an opportunity to use rich predictive forecasts directly in closed-loop robotic sampling. However, these models do not natively provide the explicit uncertainty representations assumed by classical informative-planning methods, and their forecasts often evolve in learned latent spaces rather than directly in physical ocean variables. We develop a multi-robot closed-loop adaptive sampling framework that uses a single learned generative model for forecasting, uncertainty estimation, planning, and measurement assimilation. The model forecasts an ensemble in latent space, decodes it to physical ocean states, and uses ensemble statistics to construct A- or D-optimal sampling objectives. We select sampling locations subject to robot reachability under predicted currents. The collected measurements are assimilated back into the latent state using observation-conditioned diffusion sampling. Across 120 test scenarios A- and D-optimal sampling generally outperforms static, random, and systematic-coverage baselines while adding little planning overhead. Our experiments uncover several scenarios in which model uncertainty diverges from forecast error, motivating future work in uncertainty quantification.

items.title: ZipDrift: Generating Multimodal Short-Horizon MPC Costs with One-Step Drifting Models
items.summary: Short-horizon model predictive control (MPC) is fast but myopic. ZipMPC compensates by learning a context-dependent correction of the short-horizon cost that imitates a long-horizon expert. We observe that the optimal correction is often multimodal: when a slower opponent can be passed on either side, good corrections of opposite sign coexist, and the expert's choice between them hinges on tiny cost differences. Deterministic regression then averages modes or inherits inconsistent expert tie-breaking. We propose ZipDrift, which trains a one-step drifting generator over MPC cost corrections, tilted toward low closed-loop cost and learned only from cost evaluations of candidate corrections, without differentiating through the optimiser. A few generated candidates are ranked by a learned critic, and the model-based MPC then enforces dynamics and constraints. In a kinematic overtaking benchmark derived from ZipMPC, 53% of contexts are bimodal and the manual short-horizon MPC crashes in 28.5% of test episodes. With an eight-dimensional stagewise correction, ZipDrift is collision-free in all 600 test episodes and matches the best evaluated candidate, whereas an idealised ZipMPC-style regressor crashes in 4.0% (16.0% with inconsistent expert labels) and critic-ranked random candidates with the same budget in 2.0%.

items.title: Diversity-Aware Experience Replay via Statistical Leverage Scores
items.summary: Off-policy deep reinforcement learning trains on random samples from a replay buffer of past experience. In physical robot settings, that buffer is dominated by routine: thousands of near-identical transitions from normal operation, while the rare events that define the edges of the task are rarely sampled. We propose scoring every stored transition by its statistical leverage, which measures how unusual it is relative to the buffer's own data, computed from the stored numbers alone, with no labels, rewards, or value network. We draw each mini-batch from a mixture of this score and uniform sampling. First, the natural way to build the score along the directions where the data varies most turns out to be blind when actions are stored as one-hot indicators, because indicator columns always win the variance ranking; we instead select the feature columns with the heaviest tails (largest kurtosis) where small far-away populations are revealed. Second, the importance weights that prioritized replay uses to keep gradients unbiased cancel the method exactly: with full correction, training matches uniform sampling, so we drop the correction and deliberately optimize the rebalanced objective. Third, when the rare situations of a log are relational, visible only in how a stretch of behavior relates to its goal, not in any single stored coordinate-per-transition scores are blind; applying the same tail rule to short trajectory windows described relative to their goal restores the signal, and on a three-joint arm that must push an object around an obstacle it raises the rare-task success from 0.49 to 0.69 against a labeled-oracle ceiling of 0.74.

items.title: LumiTac: Compact, High-Rate Six-Axis Optical Tactile Sensing for Human-Robot Interaction
items.summary: Integrating six-axis tactile feedback into robotic interfaces requires compact sensors with accurate load measurement and rapid online reconstruction. This paper presents LumiTac, a low-profile, camera-free optoelectronic tactile sensor combining spatially distributed illumination with spectral encoding. Five photoemitters and five RGBW photoreceivers are mounted on opposing circuit boards coupled through translucent silicone. Load-induced interlayer motion modulates the internal light field under compression, shear, bending, and torsion. The sensing head measures 12 mm in diameter and 4.75 mm in thickness, weighs less than 2 g, and has a component cost of approximately USD 7. A compact multilayer perceptron reconstructs three force and three moment components from 20 optical channels. Independent testing yielded coefficients of determination (R-squared) of 0.9657-0.9941, with mean absolute errors of 0.054-0.190 N for forces and 0.304-1.419 mN m for moments. Online prediction achieved an average update rate of 303.57 Hz and a median software processing latency of 0.722 ms. Experiments involving combined loading, light weights, and rapid tapping evaluated load tracking, sensitivity to small forces, and transient response, respectively. Robotic demonstrations further validated its applicability to tactile-guided manipulation and physical human-robot interaction. This study paves the way for compact, high-rate optical tactile sensing in robotic manipulation and human-robot interaction.

items.title: Learning Object-Centric Motion Priors from Human for Robotic Dexterous Manipulation
items.summary: Manipulating diverse objects with multi-fingered dexterous hands is challenging due to the high dimensionality and complex dynamics. Human-Object Interaction (HOI) datasets provide rich knowledge about task information and embodied interactions. Instead of solely imitating the human demonstrations, our method learns to holistically predict future hand-object states by leveraging these datasets. The predicted future states of the object can serve as a general-purpose reward term for reinforcement learning, reducing reliance on task-specific reward engineering and enhancing generalization across tasks. We conduct extensive experiments on three manipulation tasks in simulation and the real world. Our approach outperforms existing SOTA methods in both success rate and generalizability on novel objects. Furthermore, we validate the cross-embodiment compatibility of our methods by successfully deploying the skills on different robot hands.

items.title: 3D Pose Estimation in Projection Space via Pixel-level Visible Light Communication
items.summary: Projector-based augmented reality enables natural interaction between users and devices by overlaying digital information onto the physical world through projected imagery. A key technical requirement of such systems is accurate positional alignment between the projector and the devices. Pixel-level Visible Light Communication (PVLC) achieves this alignment without external sensing infrastructure by embedding invisible spatial codes into each projected pixel through high-speed brightness modulation that preserves image quality. However, the information that PVLC transmits is inherently planar. PVLC has therefore been limited to devices moving on a flat surface and cannot estimate the 3D pose of devices in three-dimensional space, such as aerial robots. To extend PVLC-based pose estimation to three dimensions, we formulate it as a Perspective-n-Point (PnP) problem. The 2D pixel positions that four coplanar photosensors on the device receive via PVLC serve as the image points, and their known 3D layout provides the object points. Experiments show that the proposed system estimates 3D pose with a latency of approximately 8~ms and a 3D position RMSE of 19.2~mm after Kalman filtering. These results confirm the first realization of real-time 3D pose estimation coordinated with high-quality projected image content without external sensing infrastructure.

items.title: A Layered View of LLM Support in Underwater Robotics
items.summary: This extended abstract discusses a specific and, in our experience, practically relevant role for large language models (LLMs) in underwater robotics. Our main premise is that, in underwater fielding missions, the immediate difficulty is often not the synthesis of new low-level control laws, but the operation of complex robotic systems under limited communications, partial observability, and expensive field time. In particular, a significant fraction of the effort during sea trials is devoted to fault diagnosis, telemetry interpretation, mission adjustment, and coordination across heterogeneous assets and operators. We argue that LLMs may be useful at this higher operational level, especially when grounded in structured vehicle state, alarms, logs, mission context, and existing planning or validation tools. At the same time, current limitations in grounding, consistency, and causal reasoning make these systems lack the predictability required to guarantee direct control, especially in real-world critical applications, although we do not exclude a future evolution in this direction. This viewpoint suggests a layered architecture in which conventional autonomy remains responsible for control, perception, estimation, and validated mission execution, whereas LLM-based modules serve as an additional support layer for debugging, operator interaction, constrained replanning support, orchestration, and post-mission analysis.

items.title: Can Astra Solve RoboMME without Breaking the Bank?
items.summary: Robotic manipulation often requires remembering information that is no longer visible, such as an object's location before occlusion or the order of a demonstrated action sequence. A large vision-language planner can read this history, but calling it before every action chunk is slow and costly. We present a three-tier system for the RoboMME benchmark. GPT-6 Astra (System 2) selects a grounded subtask from stored visual history, a $\pi_{0.5}$ vision-language-action policy (System 1) executes it, and a fine-tuned Qwen3-VL-4B monitor (System 1.5) checks after each action chunk whether the subtask is finished. The instruction is kept until the monitor reports completion or a task-specific event occurs, while the policy keeps acting on new observations. On RoboMME, the system succeeds in 79.13% of episodes with an average of 3.63 Astra calls and 80.84 seconds per episode. This is 34.62 points above the best published non-oracle baseline and 4.95 points below GroundSG+Oracle, which gives the low-level policy ground-truth subgoals.

items.title: Beyond Terminal Constraints: Reliable Robot Control with Learned Safe Sets
items.summary: Ensuring safety in advanced robot control methods such as Model Predictive Control (MPC) and Reinforcement Learning remains an open challenge. A common approach relies on control-invariant sets, yet their exact computation for nonlinear systems is generally intractable, and numerical approximations compromise theoretical guarantees. In this work, we show that safety does not need to rely exclusively on control invariance. We introduce novel classes of safe sets, each broader than classical control-invariant sets, and analyze corresponding MPC schemes that guarantee recursive feasibility by constraining different nodes of the prediction horizon rather than only the terminal state. Furthermore, when the safe set is an inner approximation of a suitable control-invariant set, our methods can ensure safety through a safe-abort strategy, even in the absence of recursive feasibility. We validate our approaches in extensive simulations on a 6-joint robot manipulator, showing fewer constraint violations than state-of-the-art methods while maintaining comparable tracking performance and computational efficiency. Hardware experiments further demonstrate the practicality of our schemes for real-world robotic applications.

items.title: Corridor-Based Monitoring and Emergency Braking Decision for Automated Vehicle Safety
items.summary: This paper addresses emergency-braking decisions for a redundant safety channel in automated vehicles. The channel is responsible for identifying hazards from sensor data and determining whether braking is necessary, given the constrained computational resources of embedded hardware. We present an emergency-braking approach that uses a predicted motion corridor to filter \ac{lidar} measurements and then decide whether the ego vehicle must brake. \ac{pmcm} constructs a curvature-aware boundary from the planned path and vehicle geometry so that the monitored region contains the full swept body on both straight and curved paths. \ac{gdeta} then decides whether the ego vehicle must command an emergency brake for objects inside this boundary, scoring geometric occupancy and temporal urgency independently. Hard gates permit braking when either source is conclusive; soft-OR arbitration combines partial evidence when neither gate is active. Consecutive-scan confirmation reduces sensitivity to transient measurement noise. Corridor coverage is evaluated in controlled collision simulations and recorded campus driving. Braking decisions are evaluated in Monte Carlo simulations of lead-vehicle braking and transverse-crossing encounters.

items.title: The brutal 2026 attack ads even rivals had to respect
items.summary: Top party strategists may hate seeing one of their candidates gutted by a brutal ad. But they can still admire the hit. Why it matters: A record $11.6 billion has plastered political ads across screens of every size in the country during the 2026 midterms . Only a handful of those earned the grudging respect of operatives on both sides. 📺 Zoom in: Multiple Republican strategists singled out the "brutal" series of ads attacking Sen. Roger Marshall (R-Kans.) over lawsuits against patients with overdue medical bills — some of whom were later arrested . Against the advice of his own team, Marshall released a self-directed ad answering the attacks. In Nebraska , an ad highlighting a past vote by former Gov. Pete Ricketts to pardon a man convicted of rape was singled out by both parties as one of the cycle's most damaging. Ricketts is expected to win re-election to the Senate. In Maine, an upbeat jingle hit Democratic nominee Troy Jackson for having children with his second cousin. "If he'll f**k his own family, he'll f**k yours too," the radio ad said (among other things). Sen. Susan Collins (R-Maine) called for the ad to be taken down. And in Florida , Rep. María Salazar (R-Fla.) turned on her own party leader, criticizing President Trump over ICE's aggressive enforcement tactics, saying some immigration policies had "gone too far." The intrigue : Even hardened operatives are dealing with a new frontier: AI-generated attack ads that can make up scenarios and put words in an opponent's mouth. In Michigan , a Republican-aligned super PAC used AI-generated imagery to depict Democratic candidate Abdul El-Sayed in a fabricated family photo and playing a game with cards referencing "Death to America" and 9/11. In Texas, GOP Senate nominee Ken Paxton's team used AI to depict Democratic candidate James Talarico defacing a Bible with a crayon and saying: "In the beginning God was non-binary, and he wasn't a Christian. And God said, 'let there be six genders,' and there were." 🤺 Between the lines: An attack ad helped spark this weekend's blowup in the Michigan Senate race. Rep. Haley Stevens' (D-Mich.) shocking decision to withdraw support from El-Sayed grew out of their public dispute over an ad she called antisemitic. El-Sayed ultimately disavowed the ad but said Stevens wasn't welcome at his events, and she endorsed former Rep. Mike Rogers (R-Mich.) on Sunday. The other side: It's hard to imagine a bigger backfire than Vivek Ramaswamy's (R) ad featuring the estranged mother of his opponent for Ohio governor, Amy Acton (D). It could prove fatal for his gubernatorial bid, and Republicans worry it could hurt Sen. John Husted's (R) re-election chances too. The ad sparked immediate bipartisan backlash. Ramaswamy doubled down before pulling it off-air. One internal GOP poll had Acton's lead grow by 6 points after the ad ran.

items.title: Potential improvements to HowTruthful and its agent skills
items.summary: I followed my own instructions for exploring Massachusetts 2026 ballot question arguments. I figured out how I want to vote. I also figured out some improvements to make to HowTruthful and its associated agent skills . Since users are rating statements' truthfulness on a 1-5 scale, it's not very useful to have a hedged statement like "Massachusetts legislators who run unopposed can take voters for granted and ignore important issues." If the rest of the statement is even a possibility, the word "can" makes the statement as a whole true. The AI skill should change such statements into a definitive form like "Massachusetts legislators who run unopposed will take voters for granted and ignore important issues." Then the user can rate that statement false, dubious, debatable, plausible, or true. There was a contest where I was among the winners , even though I disagreed with the organizers' vision of having AI assess truthfulness. In my contest entry I opined that humans should do the final assessment; AI's role would stop at ingesting and structuring arguments. (More on the contest in a future post.) Having just gone through 400 or so statements in order to figure out how to vote, my position has shifted. I think it would make sense, in the course of a human's dialogue with an AI, for the AI to offer to put a set of truthfulness ratings onto a set of statements in response to that dialogue. A human could accept such an offer and save work. Related to the previous point, the one-way process I've set up isn't good enough. An AI ingests and structures arguments. You have a dialogue with it to refine the arguments. Then you import them into HowTruthful where you assess truthfulness. While I was assessing ballot questions, there were several points where I wanted to go back and use AI assistance to improve the argument tree. Having rated a lot of statements, I didn't want to start over with everything marked debatable. I wanted to start from the partially-rated argument graph. I could do that easily if I had an export button on the main ballot-questions statement. But all I have is an export page for all my private opinions. Manually extracting the right part of that export is clumsy. That missing export function also makes it clumsy for me to share with you my reasoning for how to vote on the ballot questions. But if anybody asks me to, I'll put it together. Discuss

items.title: The Generative Gap Between Speculative Drafter and Continuous Diffusion Language Model
items.summary: This research paper explores the generative gap between speculative drafters and continuous diffusion language models, comparing their efficiency in language generation and typical evaluation methods. It analyzes how CDLMs generate independently through iterative refinement versus drafters proposing text for verification.

items.title: Adaptive Personalization Under Preference Epistemic Uncertainty
items.summary: This research explores adaptive personalization for conversational AI, focusing on how systems can adapt their response strategies to evolving human preferences under epistemic uncertainty. It addresses the challenge of dynamic preferences rather than relying on static memory recall.

items.title: Fewer Heads, Fewer Memories: Pruning Redundant Attention Heads Suppresses Verbatim Memorisation
items.summary: This research suggests that pruning redundant attention heads in large language models can suppress verbatim memorization of training data, which raises concerns about privacy and intellectual property. It investigates how attention mechanisms contribute to this behavior.

items.title: EDU-Jev Training System-One Decision Models for Education
items.summary: This paper introduces the EDU-Jev Training System, which utilizes generative language models to create one-decision models for automated decisions in education. These models can perform tasks such as assigning rubric scores or identifying errors in student solutions.

items.title: HyperRepair: Recovering Forgotten General Capabilities of Fine-Tuned Language Models
items.summary: This paper introduces HyperRepair, a framework designed to recover the general capabilities of fine-tuned language models, which are often weakened during domain specialization. It addresses the trade-off between domain performance and preserving broader functionalities.

items.title: S2TDR: Structured Multimodal Reconstruction for Sticker-Aware Dialogue Understanding
items.summary: This research proposes S2TDR, a structured multimodal reconstruction method for sticker-aware dialogue understanding, to interpret the non-literal and context-dependent meanings of stickers in social media. It aims to improve AI's comprehension of affect, stance, and intent beyond literal text.

items.title: Beyond Response Scoring: An AI-aware Cognitive Supervision Framework for Automated Mathematical Short Answer Grading
items.summary: This research proposes an AI-aware cognitive supervision framework for automated mathematical short answer grading, moving beyond simple response scoring. It aims to enable transformer-based language models to better comprehend, reason about, and evaluate complex mathematical answers.

items.title: PsyInterviewee: Informational Invariance and Relational Adaptivity in Mental Health Interview Simulation
items.summary: This paper introduces PsyInterviewee, an LLM-based simulated interviewee designed for mental health interview simulation, focusing on informational invariance and relational adaptivity. It supports interviewer training and evaluation of mental health interviewing systems beyond mere human-likeness.

items.title: Comparative Evaluation of LLM-Based Review Paradigms for Academic Paper Quality Assessment
items.summary: This study comparatively evaluates different paradigms for using large language models (LLMs) to support the peer review process for academic paper quality assessment.

items.title: KV-Cache Patching: Tracing How and Where Fine-Tuned Behaviors Arise
items.summary: This research uses KV-Cache Patching to trace where and how fine-tuned behaviors arise within language models, aiming to better understand their internal mechanisms.

items.title: Enhancing Knowledge Entity Relation Extraction in Abstracts and Full-text Content of Academic Articles Using Large Language Models
items.summary: This study investigates the effectiveness of large language models (LLMs) for knowledge entity relation extraction (KERE) from the abstracts and full-text content of academic articles.

items.title: CEFR Level Assessment across Languages and Text Granularities
items.summary: This research addresses the challenges in automatic assessment of textual CEFR levels across languages and text granularities, a key task in educational natural language processing.

items.title: Text as an Index for Zero-Shot Cross-Domain Knowledge Tracing
items.summary: This research explores using text as an index for zero-shot cross-domain knowledge tracing, a method for predicting student responses without prior training data for new educational platforms.

items.title: The psychophysics of affect in large language models
items.summary: This research investigates the psychophysics of affect in large language models, exploring how LLMs map outcomes to feelings and utilize these mappings in decision-making contexts like gambling.

items.title: Spatial Atlas-Informed Loss Ensembles for Whole-Body PSMA PET/CT Metastasis Segmentation
items.summary: This paper investigates integrating population metastasis atlases into model training to improve whole-body PSMA PET/CT prostate metastasis segmentation, which typically relies only on images.

items.title: AquaProbe: Efficient Adaptation of Frozen Vision Models for Underwater Images
items.summary: AquaProbe proposes efficient methods to adapt pre-trained vision models for reliable visual perception in challenging underwater environments, crucial for autonomous underwater exploration.

items.title: Sparse Autoencoders for Expert-Assisted Interpretation of Histopathology Foundation Model Embeddings
items.summary: This research explores using sparse autoencoders to interpret embeddings from histopathology foundation models, aiming for concept-level understanding relevant to pathologists' reasoning patterns.

items.title: WebOverlay: High-Throughput Vision-Only Distillation for Extreme Aspect-Ratio Web Overlay Detection
items.summary: WebOverlay proposes a high-throughput, vision-only distillation method for detecting web overlays like cookie banners, offering a more efficient alternative to costly multimodal Large Language Models for automated web crawlers.

items.title: Segment Anything Pancreas: A Unified MRI Segmentation Model for Pancreatic Cancer Radiotherapy
items.summary: Pancreas-MedNeXt is proposed as a unified MRI segmentation model for pancreatic cancer radiotherapy, addressing data scarcity by segmenting the whole pancreas, its subregions, and tumors.

items.title: Grounding Image Composition with Label-Conditioned Visual Evidence
items.summary: This work introduces a method for grounding image composition labels, such as 'center' or 'rule of thirds', by associating specific visual regions with these descriptive classes.

items.title: An Empirical Study on Learning Rooftop Solar Potential from Satellite Imagery Directly Without Explicit Geometry
items.summary: Direct Rooftop Solar Prediction (DRSP) is proposed as an end-to-end method that directly estimates rooftop solar potential from satellite imagery and regional data, bypassing explicit roof geometry reconstruction.

items.title: MotorSense: A Video-EMG Dataset of Motoric Representations for Action Understanding
items.summary: MotorSense introduces the first large-scale dataset pairing egocentric video with surface electromyography (EMG) signals, enabling computer vision models to learn hand actions from embodied motor representations.

items.title: Beyond CLIP: Calibrated (Few-Shot) Defect Detection With System One Decision Models
items.summary: This research explores using calibrated decision models with vision transformers like CLIP for few-shot defect detection in manufacturing, reducing the need for extensive image datasets of defective products.

items.title: Hawkeye: Reading Illegible Text with Vision Language Models
items.summary: Hawkeye introduces a method to enable Vision-Language Models to accurately read illegible text degraded by motion blur or low resolution, particularly benefiting egocentric applications.

items.title: ReVEAL: Eliciting Role-Aware Latent Visual Evidence from MLLMs for Reasoning Video Object Segmentation
items.summary: ReVEAL presents a decoupled method using MLLMs to extract role-aware visual evidence for reasoning video object segmentation, avoiding costly cross-model alignment in the process.

items.title: GenDSR: Transferring Representations from Video Generation Models for Dynamic Spatial Reasoning
items.summary: GenDSR proposes transferring representations from video generation models to improve dynamic spatial reasoning in vision-language models. This method aims to help VLMs preserve scene state and track evolving spatial relations over time.

items.title: Task-Performance Routing for Multi-Teacher Distillation in CT Medical Image Segmentation
items.summary: This research presents a task-performance routing method for multi-teacher distillation in CT medical image segmentation. It aims to combine the complementary strengths of pre-trained models more effectively by accounting for variations in teacher accuracy across organs and regions.

items.title: Queryable Gaussian View Index: Text Retrieval and Selective Camera Localization
items.summary: Queryable Gaussian View Index (QGVI) is presented for text retrieval and selective camera localization within Gaussian scene assets. It allows querying existing 3D assets and their calibrated data, enabling text-view retrieval and returning camera poses in the asset's coordinate frame.

items.title: Parse Before You Execute: Efficient Spatial Reasoning with Executable Primitives
items.summary: This research proposes "Parse Before You Execute," a method for efficient spatial reasoning in Vision-Language Models (VLMs) using executable primitives. It aims to improve tool-integrated pipelines by grounding computation in explicit geometry.

items.title: SACQ: Structure-Aware Codebook Quantization for Ultra-Low-Bit Vision-Language-Action Models
items.summary: SACQ introduces Structure-Aware Codebook Quantization for ultra-low-bit Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models. This method aims to reduce the memory footprint of VLA models, making them more suitable for deployment on resource-constrained robotic platforms.

items.title: Beyond Trial-and-Error: A Geospatial-Guided Active Reasoning Framework for Robust Aerial Vision-and-Language Navigation
items.summary: This research presents a geospatial-guided active reasoning framework for robust Aerial Vision-and-Language Navigation (VLN). It aims to improve UAVs' ability to locate language-specified goals in large-scale urban environments, moving beyond reactive paradigms.

items.title: Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning of Transformer Encoders for Audio-Image-Symbolic Music Retrieval
items.summary: This paper investigates the effectiveness of parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT) of transformer encoders for audio-image-symbolic music retrieval. The goal is to create compatible and discriminative representations across different music modalities.

items.title: TACO: Trajectory-Aware Curvature Observation for Memorization Localization and Mitigation in Diffusion Models
items.summary: TACO introduces Trajectory-Aware Curvature Observation for localizing and mitigating memorization in text-to-image diffusion models. This method aims to precisely identify and address instances where models reproduce memorized training content within localized image regions.

items.title: Scout-Refine-Correct: Teaching Flow Models to Refine Their Own Samples
items.summary: Scout-Refine-Correct is a new training recipe designed to teach flow models to refine their own generated samples. This method aims to improve the quality of image generation models beyond what is typically achieved through sampling steps alone.

items.title: Attention Maps Know When to Think: Training-Free Difficulty-Aware Chain-of-Thought for Reasoning Segmentation
items.summary: This research introduces a training-free, difficulty-aware Chain-of-Thought method for reasoning segmentation in Multi-modal Large Language Models (MLLMs), utilizing attention maps. It aims to prevent performance degradation caused by indiscriminate CoT usage.

items.title: GRIT: Gradient Masking for Visually Misgrounded Tokens in Text-Rich Reasoning
items.summary: GRIT proposes Gradient Masking to address visually misgrounded tokens in text-rich reasoning tasks for vision-language models (VLMs). This method aims to improve the effectiveness of reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards in such scenarios.

items.title: TADP: Dual-Branch Temporally Adaptive Differential Privacy for Expression-Aware Video Anonymization
items.summary: TADP is a temporally adaptive differential privacy framework for expression-aware video anonymization and inference-time privacy-preserving video generation. It uses a dual-branch design to extract, clip, and privatize identity and expression representations.

items.title: A Self-Supervised Pose Estimation Approach for Construction Machines
items.summary: This paper introduces a self-supervised, three-stage approach for pose estimation of construction machines. This method addresses the challenge of requiring massive labeled datasets common in supervised pose estimation.

items.title: OT-CAL: Optimal-Transport-Guided Adaptive Sample Selection for Efficient Visual Learning
items.summary: OT-CAL introduces an Optimal-Transport-Guided Adaptive Sample Selection method for efficient visual learning in deep neural networks. It aims to optimize training by selectively choosing samples that contribute most effectively to learning, addressing the varying utility of mini-batch samples.

items.title: Retrieval-Augmented Initialization with Dual-Guided Inversion for Flow-Based Inverse Problem Solvers
items.summary: This research introduces a novel method called Retrieval-Augmented Initialization with Dual-Guided Inversion, which improves the initialization of flow-based generative models for solving inverse problems, such as image reconstruction.

items.title: Nereus: A Large-Scale Underwater Dataset for Fine-Grained Attribute Understanding and Grounded Counting Perception
items.summary: This paper presents Nereus, a large-scale underwater dataset designed for fine-grained attribute understanding and grounded counting perception, supporting applications like ecological conservation and fishery monitoring by enabling models to recognize biological traits.

items.title: SAR-TS-BERT: Physics-Guided Self-Supervised Pre-Training With Polarimetric Features for SAR Time-Series Crop Classification
items.summary: This research introduces SAR-TS-BERT, a physics-guided self-supervised pre-training method that uses polarimetric features from multitemporal synthetic aperture radar (SAR) imagery to improve crop classification for agricultural monitoring.

items.title: Hard Sample-Conditioned Decorrelated Attention for Robust Face Recognition
items.summary: This research proposes Hard Sample-Conditioned Decorrelated Attention, a novel mechanism for Vision Transformers (ViTs) that encourages head disentanglement and improves robustness in face recognition by preventing redundant attention patterns.

items.title: Adaptive Coverage Algorithms for Mobile Ad Hoc Networks in Dynamic Worlds
items.summary: This paper presents adaptive coverage algorithms for coordinating mobile agents in dynamic and unknown environments, extending a framework for the Partially Observable Cooperative Guard Art Gallery Problem.

items.title: Proof-Carrying Evolution: Black-Box Search, White-Box Flight
items.summary: Proof-Carrying Evolution investigates whether language models can aid in designing formally verifiable controllers by proposing controllers along with their certificates and numerical parameters.

items.title: Hierarchical World Models with Implicit Dynamics
items.summary: This paper explores hierarchical world models with implicit dynamics to improve planning for embodied agents in long-horizon tasks, addressing cumulative errors and search complexity.

items.title: HSBC to open Hong Kong AI Institute following Singapore launch - Reuters
items.summary: HSBC is establishing an AI Institute in Hong Kong, following a similar launch in Singapore, to advance artificial intelligence research and applications within the bank.

items.title: Anthropic’s Claude slashes pharmaceutical document review times by 89% - TechRadar
items.summary: Anthropic's Claude AI model has been applied to pharmaceutical document review, leading to a reported 89% reduction in review times.

items.title: Macquarie Executive Sees AI Fast-Tracking Junior Analyst Careers - Bloomberg.com
items.summary: A Macquarie executive predicts that AI will accelerate career advancement for junior analysts in the financial industry by enhancing their capabilities.

items.title: Competition in Generative AI: Evidence from Consumer Demand (NBER)
items.summary: A National Bureau of Economic Research (NBER) paper presents findings on competition within the generative AI market, based on evidence from consumer demand.

items.title: Argentina most exposed to AI impact in Latin America
items.summary: A study finds that Argentina is the Latin American country most exposed to the impact of artificial intelligence.

items.title: Early Career Researcher Responses to AI in Math
items.summary: This arXiv article examines how early career researchers in mathematics are responding to and engaging with artificial intelligence in their academic work.

items.title: Claude AI Predicts a Huge Move for Nvidia (NVDA) in Euphoric Scenario - Tokenist
items.summary: Claude AI was used to predict a significant movement for Nvidia's stock under a "euphoric scenario," demonstrating a real-world application of AI models in financial market analysis.

items.title: Is your chatbot less helpful because it thinks you’re a bad person? — Replicating a blogpost
items.summary: An experiment replicated a previous finding, investigating whether large language models like Claude Opus 5.5 and GPT-6 variants provide less helpful answers if they perceive the user as a "bad person," yielding different results. This explores bias and model behavior.
