items.title: Prospect Theory in Large Language Models: A Meta-Analysis of Loss Aversion, Diminishing Sensitivity, and Probability Weighting
items.summary: A meta-analysis exploring the application of prospect theory, including loss aversion and diminishing sensitivity, to decision-making within large language models.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence in Mechanical Engineering: Foundations, Opportunities, Challenges, and Responsibilities
items.summary: An article discussing the foundational aspects, opportunities, challenges, and responsibilities of artificial intelligence in mechanical engineering.

items.title: Scaling Qualitative Analysis with Large Language Models: Development and Validation of the Smart Coder Framework for Human-LLM Collaborative Coding
items.summary: Presents the Smart Coder Framework, a new three-phase approach for structuring human-LLM collaborative coding in qualitative analysis.

items.title: Distilling Expert Judgment at Scale
items.summary: Describes a general methodology for distilling expert human judgment into automated evaluation systems for high-stakes AI model applications.

items.title: Scoped Semantic Invariance as a Foundation for LLM Reliability
items.summary: Formalizes 'scoped semantic invariance' as a theoretical foundation for improving the reliability and consistency of large language models.

items.title: AI Teaches Humans to Handle Complexity in the Game of Go
items.summary: A study using the game of Go to investigate how AI can teach humans to balance local stability and global coordination in complex strategic decision-making.

items.title: Data Optimization for LLMs: A Survey
items.summary: A survey paper providing an overview of current strategies and advancements in data optimization techniques specifically for Large Language Models.

items.title: BoardSafety: AI-Ready Data from Manufacturer Documentation for Development-Board Safety
items.summary: This work investigates using LLMs to determine the safety of operations for specific development boards by extracting and leveraging data from manufacturer documentation, assisting hardware experiments.

items.title: A Comprehensive Framework for All Stages of Large-Model Training: From Data and Tokenization, through Pretraining, to Post-Training Alignment
items.summary: This paper presents a comprehensive framework outlining all stages of large model training for LLMs and MLLMs, covering data, tokenization, pretraining, and post-training alignment techniques like SFT and RL.

items.title: The Future Is Finer: Multivariate Time Series Super-Resolution Forecasting
items.summary: This research proposes a multivariate time series super-resolution forecasting method to enable finer-grained decision-making from coarsely archived data on web platforms.

items.title: When Generated Information Returns: Error Persistence in LLM-Mediated Information Ecosystems
items.summary: This research investigates error persistence in LLM-mediated information ecosystems, analyzing how generated information circulates and can lead to errors feeding back into subsequent model generations.

items.title: Graph-dependent pooling: adaptive granularity in hierarchical graph neural networks
items.summary: This paper introduces graph-dependent pooling, a method for hierarchical graph neural networks to achieve adaptive granularity in learning multi-level structural representations, overcoming limitations of fixed pooling ratios.

items.title: RAQ-MLA: Role-Aware Quantization for Multi-Head Latent Attention Caches
items.summary: This research proposes RAQ-MLA, a role-aware quantization technique for Multi-Head Latent Attention Caches, aiming to optimize the compressed key-value latent in frontier large language models.

items.title: TAD: Distilling Vision-Language-Action Policies from Teacher Trajectories Alone
items.summary: This research proposes TAD (Trajectory-only Adversarial Distillation), a method for distilling vision-language-action policies from teacher trajectories alone, addressing the limitation of relying on exposed teacher action scores.

items.title: Jointly Modeling Preferences and Imperfect Decision-Making in Large Language Models
items.summary: This paper explores how to jointly model preferences and imperfect decision-making in large language models, investigating whether expressed preferences predict their strategic behavior in agentic interactions.

items.title: Physics-Informed Graph-Based Safe RL with Constraint-Specific Critics for Community Battery Coordination in Distribution Network
items.summary: This paper proposes a physics-informed graph-based safe reinforcement learning approach with constraint-specific critics for coordinating community batteries in distribution networks to manage voltage and line-limit violations.

items.title: Power-of-Two Leaky Integrate-and-Fire Neurons for Event-Driven Vision-Language-Action Inference
items.summary: This research proposes using Power-of-Two Leaky Integrate-and-Fire Neurons for event-driven Vision-Language-Action (VLA) inference, aiming to enable energy-constrained deployment for robotic manipulation by leveraging sparse computation.

items.title: All the Facts, Still the Wrong Answer: Integration Gaps in Vision-Language Models
items.summary: This paper investigates integration gaps in vision-language models, where models fail at multimodal reasoning despite possessing individual facts, by studying how they combine evidence. The research aims to clarify whether failures stem from reading facts or from their combined use.

items.title: Local Entropy Fluctuations for Black-Box LLM-Generated Text Detection
items.summary: This research proposes using local entropy fluctuations for black-box detection of LLM-generated text in a zero-shot setting. This method aims to overcome limitations of existing dual-model and resampling-based detectors that struggle with unprompted continuations.

items.title: An actively trained neural operator for near-explicit atmospheric chemistry
items.summary: This research introduces an actively trained neural operator as a neural emulator to make near-explicit atmospheric chemistry mechanisms computationally feasible within Earth-system models. This method aims to advance chemistry in longer time steps than previous approaches.

items.title: Are We Done with UMLS Injection into Language Models for Medical Question Answering?
items.summary: This research investigates the ongoing utility of injecting the Unified Medical Language System (UMLS) into language models for medical question answering. It questions whether this approach, which uses knowledge graphs, remains optimal for enhancing factual accuracy and reasoning traceability in medical AI.

items.title: The Path to NDE 4.0: A Review of Algorithms, Techniques, and Strategies for Autonomous Inspection
items.summary: This paper provides a comprehensive review of algorithms, techniques, and strategies for autonomous inspection in Non-Destructive Inspection (NDI), a critical aspect of quality assurance. It analyzes the current landscape to outline the path towards NDE 4.0.

items.title: Towards Adversarially Robust Multigraph Neural Networks for Financial Crime Analysis
items.summary: This research focuses on developing adversarially robust multigraph neural networks tailored for financial crime analysis, leveraging the multigraph structure of financial transaction networks. These networks aim to achieve strong performance on anti-money laundering tasks by explicitly modeling distinct edges for repeated transactions.

items.title: End-to-End Differentiable Diffusion Conditioning for Physics-Informed Optimization
items.summary: This research introduces an end-to-end differentiable diffusion conditioning method for physics-informed optimization of high-dimensional physical systems. This approach addresses challenges in offline model-based optimization by improving designs using fixed datasets without test-time access to the true objective.

items.title: Autoregressive Multimodal Anomaly Detection with Large Language Models for Microservice Systems
items.summary: This research proposes an autoregressive multimodal anomaly detection method utilizing large language models for microservice systems. This approach aims to improve the reliability and availability of large-scale cloud applications by effectively identifying failures and performance anomalies.

items.title: When and How Does Muon Precondition? The Role of Structured Gradient Noise
items.summary: This research paper investigates the theoretical foundations and mechanisms of Muon, a popular optimizer for large language model training. It specifically studies how gradient noise geometry influences Muon's preconditioning benefits.

items.title: ConsMSA: Semantic Distribution Consistency Learning for Multimodal Sentiment Analysis
items.summary: This paper introduces ConsMSA, a new method for multimodal sentiment analysis that addresses semantic inconsistencies in raw multimodal sequences. It aims to improve sentiment prediction by integrating signals from text, video, and audio.

items.title: Efficient Omni-modal Large Language Model Inference via Per-Query Modality Selection
items.summary: This paper proposes a method for efficient inference in omni-modal large language models by dynamically selecting relevant modalities per query. The approach aims to reduce substantial inference costs while maintaining strong multimodal understanding capabilities.

items.title: Not All Retained Clients Are Equal: Client Selection for Federated Unlearning
items.summary: This paper proposes an improved client selection method for federated unlearning, aiming to efficiently remove a target client's influence from a trained model without the prohibitive cost of retraining from scratch.

items.title: PaperScorer: How Predictable Is Paper Acceptance?
items.summary: This paper explores PaperScorer, an AI system designed to predict the acceptance of research papers by modeling the complexities of human peer review. It investigates the predictability of paper acceptance given only the paper content.

items.title: CuraLoc: Repository-Level Fault Localization via Planned Code Inspection
items.summary: This paper introduces CuraLoc, a method for repository-level fault localization that uses planned code inspection to identify where code changes are needed from bug reports. It aims to improve efficiency compared to iterative model-based inspection methods.

items.title: Nested Sparsity for Scalable Pretraining and Continual Learning
items.summary: This paper proposes "Nested Sparsity" as a technique for Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) transformers to enhance scalability in pretraining and continual learning. It focuses on improving the efficiency of conditional computation in large-scale deep learning models.

items.title: Speculative Diffusion is a Tale of Two Tradeoffs
items.summary: This paper analyzes "Speculative Diffusion," a technique used to accelerate the inference speed of autoregressive large language models. It examines the tradeoffs inherent in this method, which samples from a faster, lower-quality draft model.

items.title: Rethinking Multi-View Fusion for Urban Representation Learning
items.summary: This research paper rethinks multi-view fusion techniques for urban representation learning, which encodes diverse urban signals into unified embeddings. The goal is to improve performance for downstream tasks such as check-in prediction and crime forecasting.

items.title: Cautious Conflict-Free Inverse Gradient Methods
items.summary: This paper introduces "Cautious Conflict-Free Inverse Gradient Methods" for Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs). It aims to improve the use of PINNs for modeling complex phenomena in physics and engineering by incorporating physical constraints into neural networks.

items.title: Rewriting Scaling Laws for Synthetic Data with Compute and Data Constraints
items.summary: This paper investigates the scaling laws for generating synthetic data through language model rewrites, which are used in pretraining corpora. It examines the optimal compute allocation and data constraints for effectively using synthetic data in model training.

items.title: Forecasting Associations, Not Interventions: A Preregistered Causal Audit of Covariate-Aware Time Series Foundation Models
items.summary: This paper presents a causal audit of covariate-aware time series foundation models to determine if they forecast associations or interventions. It investigates the reliability of these models when answering what-if queries, given their training on observational data.

items.title: Effectiveness of Curriculum Learning Depends on Reward Sparsity and Competing Optima
items.summary: This research investigates the factors influencing the effectiveness of curriculum learning in artificial settings, particularly focusing on reward sparsity and competing optima. It aims to explain why curriculum learning's efficacy varies between reinforcement and supervised learning.

items.title: Scaling Transformer Energy-based Models For High Quality Image Synthesis
items.summary: This paper explores scaling Transformer Energy-based Models (EBMs) to achieve high-quality image synthesis. It investigates how this class of generative models can leverage compositional generation and inference-time scaling for improved sample quality.

items.title: Learning Structured Sparsity for Large Models: Bridging Model Compressibility and Efficient Inference
items.summary: This research investigates "Structured Sparsity" as a technique to improve model compressibility and achieve efficient inference for large AI models. It addresses the computational and memory demands associated with increasing model scale, especially for deployment in constrained environments.

items.title: Topological Equivalence of Spectral and Density Cluster Hierarchies
items.summary: This paper compares the topological equivalence of spectral and density cluster hierarchies, two canonical methods for recovering hierarchical clustering from an underlying density function. It analyzes their properties and relationships in data analysis.

items.title: Decode Late, Multiply Once: Rethinking the Dot Product for Quantized Weights
items.summary: This paper proposes a new method, "Decode Late, Multiply Once," to rethink dot product computation for quantized neural networks with low-bit weights. The technique aims to significantly improve computational efficiency using fewer additions and multiplications.

items.title: Every Weight Is a Path of Shared Discrete Decisions
items.summary: This paper introduces TWIG (Tree-structured Weights with Inherited Gates), a new representation where neural network weights are defined by a path of discrete decisions, enabling shared upper paths for related weights.

items.title: Agreement rather than normalisation keeps depth reusable in looped language models
items.summary: This paper investigates whether the reusability of depth in looped language models, allowing for inference beyond trained loop steps, depends on state normalization or an agreement mechanism between loop steps.

items.title: Towards Trustworthy AI-Enabled Emergency Medical Dispatch: Uncertainty-Aware Ambulance Travel Time Estimation
items.summary: This research focuses on developing trustworthy AI for emergency medical dispatch by improving ambulance travel time estimation through uncertainty-aware methods to enhance timely resource allocation.

items.title: A Mathematical Theory of the Jacobian Lens
items.summary: This paper presents a mathematical theory for the Jacobian lens, an interpretability tool introduced by Anthropic, which identifies linear directions in language model hidden states resembling working memory representations.

items.title: Beyond Heuristics and Commercial Navigation: An AI-Augmented Decision-Support for Ambulance Travel Time Estimation
items.summary: This work proposes an AI-augmented decision-support system for ambulance travel time estimation, aiming to improve accuracy beyond current heuristic and commercial navigation methods for emergency medical dispatch.

items.title: REDAR: Reinforcement-Driven Adaptive Regularisation for Class Incremental Learning
items.summary: This paper introduces REDAR (Reinforcement-Driven Adaptive Regularisation), a method that uses reinforcement learning to adapt regularization coefficients for class-incremental learning, improving the stability-plasticity trade-off.

items.title: GS-MoE: Training-Free MoE Compression via Groupwise Subspace Sharing and Pruning
items.summary: This paper introduces GS-MoE, a training-free compression framework for Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models that reduces memory bottlenecks by addressing redundancy across and within experts through subspace sharing and pruning.

items.title: PRISM: Promoting Sampling Diversity of Large Language Models with Implicit Stochastic Modulation
items.summary: This paper introduces PRISM, a method for promoting sampling diversity in large language models using implicit stochastic modulation to counter mode collapse and generate a wider range of semantic outputs.

items.title: ReMedI: Inference-Time Refinement and Self-Distillation for Controllable Molecular Optimization
items.summary: This paper presents ReMedI, a method utilizing inference-time refinement and self-distillation for controllable molecular optimization in drug development, aiming to improve competing properties while preserving potency.

items.title: Putting Transformer Theories to the Test
items.summary: This work systematically tests various formal theories developed to characterize the capabilities and limitations of the transformer architecture, evaluating their underlying assumptions and conceptual frameworks.

items.title: REACT: Representational Early Analysis and Control of Chain-of-Thought Trajectories
items.summary: This paper introduces REACT, a conditional activation intervention system for representational early analysis and control of Chain-of-Thought trajectories, investigating effective intervention points in reasoning models.

items.title: Beyond Data Schedule: Fast LLM Pretraining on Data Mixtures by Loss-Reweighting
items.summary: This research proposes improving fast large language model pretraining on data mixtures by using loss-reweighting to mitigate knowledge forgetting while acquiring specialized capabilities.

items.title: Rethinking LoRA Initialization for Robust Asymmetric Learning Rates
items.summary: This paper rethinks LoRA initialization to achieve robust performance with asymmetric learning rates, addressing LoRA's sensitivity to learning rate choices in fine-tuning.

items.title: Sparsity-driven emergence of functional modularity in multitask neural networks
items.summary: This research demonstrates that sparsity-inducing regularization fosters the emergence of functional modularity in multitask neural networks, helping organize shared computation into specialized components.

items.title: Curvature-Aware Clipping: Mitigating Bias in DPSGD via Approximate Second-Order Information
items.summary: This paper introduces Curvature-Aware Clipping as a method to mitigate bias in Differentially Private Stochastic Gradient Descent (DPSGD) by incorporating approximate second-order information.

items.title: CFBrainAug: Modularity-Induced Counterfactual Brain Network Augmentation for Interpretable fMRI-based Autism Diagnosis
items.summary: This paper introduces CFBrainAug, a modularity-induced counterfactual brain network augmentation method, to improve interpretable fMRI-based diagnosis of Autism Spectrum Disorder by addressing overfitting.

items.title: Dual-Adaptive Z-Score PPO: Dynamic Clipping Using Action Confidence and Normalized Advantage Magnitude
items.summary: This paper introduces Dual-Adaptive Z-Score PPO, an enhancement to the PPO algorithm that uses dynamic clipping based on action confidence and normalized advantage magnitude for improved stability.

items.title: Principia: Test-Time Hypotheses to Principle Construction for Scientific Discovery
items.summary: This paper introduces Principia, a system designed for scientific discovery that constructs empirical principles from test-time hypotheses to guide further investigation into observed phenomena.

items.title: Head Dimension Matters in Language Models for Long-Context Retrieval
items.summary: This paper investigates how head dimension in multi-head attention mechanisms impacts long-context retrieval in language models, analyzing its effect on context representation and processing efficiency.

items.title: MS-TTRL: Breaking the Frequency Conflict in Multiple-Solution Test-Time Reinforcement Learning
items.summary: This paper introduces MS-TTRL, a new method for test-time reinforcement learning designed to handle tasks with multiple valid solutions without extensive data annotation.

items.title: Correct but Unselectable: The Hidden Interface Tax in Multi-Candidate Reasoning
items.summary: This paper identifies a limitation in multi-candidate reasoning for small language models where increasing candidate generation does not always improve accuracy due to a 'hidden interface tax'.

items.title: BiLoCo: Binary Low-Rank Corrections for Post-Training Quantization
items.summary: This paper proposes BiLoCo, a new method using binary low-rank corrections to improve the accuracy of post-training FP4 quantization for large language models, reducing inference cost.

items.title: Anti-coherence Regularized Absolute Scaling for Out-of-Distribution Detection
items.summary: This paper presents 'Anti-coherence Regularized Absolute Scaling,' a novel method designed to enhance out-of-distribution detection, a critical component of AI safety.

items.title: SKG in Practice: OOD Generalization Cases Across FourDomains
items.summary: This paper details the engineering implementation of the SKG inference framework and provides case studies demonstrating its out-of-distribution generalization capabilities across four domains.

items.title: Whispering Wisely: Smart Subset Selection for ASR Fine-Tuning
items.summary: This paper introduces a method for 'smart subset selection' to efficiently fine-tune automatic speech recognition (ASR) models like OpenAI's Whisper, reducing the cost of adaptation to new domains.

items.title: Knowledge-Guided LLM for Intent-Driven Service Orchestration in Integrated Terrestrial and Non-Terrestrial 6G Networks
items.summary: This paper proposes a knowledge-guided LLM framework for intent-driven service orchestration in integrated terrestrial and non-terrestrial 6G networks to handle ambiguous natural-language service intents.

items.title: TraceQuery: learning what to recompute from full-denoising trajectory in diffusion language models
items.summary: This paper introduces 'TraceQuery,' a method to reduce the inference cost of diffusion language models by learning what parts of token representations to recompute during the denoising process.

items.title: Merge-Based Vocabulary Extension Stalls at the Pre-Tokenizer: An English-Preserving Repair for Nepali, Tested in Continued Pretraining
items.summary: This paper identifies an inefficiency in the pre-tokenization of Nepali words by LLMs like Llama-3 and Qwen3 due to Unicode letter limitations and proposes an English-preserving repair.

items.title: AdaptTok-Indic: Script-Aware Adaptive Tokenization for Indic Languages
items.summary: This paper presents AdaptTok-Indic, an Indic-specialized extension of adaptive tokenization that combines Unicode normalization to improve tokenization efficiency for Indic languages in multilingual models.

items.title: SUDO: From Scientific Publications to Global Scholarly Discourse
items.summary: This paper discusses SUDO, a framework for constructing Scholarly Knowledge Graphs (SKGs) that supports literature search, scientific discovery, and agent-assisted research by improving knowledge representation.

items.title: Conceptizer: Next-Token Prediction Is Not All You Need
items.summary: This paper introduces 'Conceptizer,' a training framework that extends next-token prediction for language models by incorporating a reward for meaning, addressing the limitations of predicting only the exact next token.

items.title: EviGround-CT: Sentence-to-Volume Grounding for Verifying LLM-Generated Chest CT Reports
items.summary: EviGround-CT is proposed to verify findings in LLM-generated chest CT reports by grounding sentences to specific volumetric evidence, addressing cases where reported findings lack localized proof.

items.title: Each Insufficient in Its Own Way: Calibrating Language Models Across Varying Evidence States
items.summary: This paper investigates how language models can be calibrated to assess the sufficiency of evidence before answering, aiming to improve their ability to decide whether to answer or gather more information.

items.title: Two Uncertainties Are Not One: Disagreement versus Decision-Risk in Cheap Structured Content Moderation
items.summary: This paper explores the distinction between disagreement and decision-risk in cost-effective content moderation, proposing a new class of "System One" models that provide typed, calibrated decisions instead of text outputs.

items.title: The Emergence and Sparsification of a Syntactic Circuit
items.summary: This research investigates the emergence and sparsification of syntactic circuits for subject-verb number agreement in Pythia language models during training, analyzing how grammatical behavior is learned and represented in neurons.

items.title: How Does Post-Training Shape LLM Value Preferences?
items.summary: This research examines how post-training shapes the value preferences of large language models, particularly how imbalanced opinion proportions in training corpora can impact representation of demographic groups.

items.title: Examining form-based linguistic productivity in people and large language models
items.summary: This study compares the form-based linguistic productivity in humans and large language models, aiming to understand the abstractness of knowledge enabling novel word use.

items.title: Perturbation-Based Data Selection for Medical Question Answering
items.summary: This research investigates perturbation-based data selection for medical question answering, aiming to efficiently adapt medical language models by identifying compact and effective training subsets.

items.title: Quantifying Meaning with SCAPE-T: Semantic Complexity from Encoder-Only Transformer Attention
items.summary: This paper introduces SCAPE-T, a novel method for quantifying semantic complexity in NLP by operationalizing it as the code length required to specify a text's meaning, utilizing encoder-only Transformer attention.

items.title: Adaptive Transfer of Representational Signatures for LLM Reliability Detection
items.summary: This research explores adaptive transfer of representational signatures to develop quality detectors for large language models, aiming to detect reliability issues like hallucinations and reasoning errors.

items.title: Propasafe-Hybrid: A Text-Based Hybrid Propaganda Detection Tool
items.summary: Propasafe-Hybrid is introduced as a text-based hybrid tool for sentence-level propaganda detection, integrating a fine-tuned transformer to identify propagandistic content in online news and social media.

items.title: Incremental Predictive Value of LLM Tutoring Interactions for Student Performance
items.summary: This study evaluates the incremental predictive value of LLM tutoring interactions for student performance, analyzing semester-level exchanges from an AI tutor to improve assignment-score prediction.

items.title: Five Architectures, One Shared Space Cross-Model Representational Alignment Without Weight Merging
items.summary: This paper investigates methods for aligning the internal representations of five independently trained language models with different architectures, without merging their weights. It explores techniques to enable cross-model understanding and combination.

items.title: Eat Your Precision: Precision Objective Mitigates Reward Hacking in Rubric-based RL
items.summary: This paper introduces a precision objective to mitigate reward hacking in rubric-based reinforcement learning, particularly for non-verifiable tasks. It addresses how current reward systems often lead models to prioritize recall over precision in their responses.

items.title: One Model, Two Paths: Balancing Single-Pass and Looped Performance in Language Models
items.summary: This research explores a method to improve language model performance by adapting pretrained models to support both single-pass and looped inference. It achieves this by reusing middle-layer weights, allowing for additional computation without adding parameters.

items.title: Words Are the Voice of the Mind: Depression Severity Estimation from Social Traces via Mental-Guided Evidence Reasoning
items.summary: This research proposes a method for estimating depression severity using social media traces, employing mental-guided evidence reasoning. It offers an alternative to traditional assessment methods by leveraging online user data for mental health insights.

items.title: Embedding-Based Educational Taxonomies
items.summary: This research explores the creation of embedding-based educational taxonomies to organize and categorize educational content, such as exercise problems, into concepts, skills, or knowledge components. These taxonomies aim to define learning objectives for intelligent tutoring systems.

items.title: StateWise: Teaching Language Models to Track and Obey Evolving Constraints in Multi-Turn Dialogue
items.summary: This research introduces StateWise, a method for teaching language models to effectively track and obey evolving constraints within multi-turn dialogues. It aims to overcome persistence and recall failures in instruction-tuned LLMs for conversational assistants.

items.title: Task Format as a Factor in Adaptation: A Controlled Comparison of LoRA and Full Fine-Tuning for Prompt-Safety Classification
items.summary: This controlled study compares the effectiveness of Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) and full fine-tuning for prompt-safety classification in language models. It investigates the impact of task format as a factor in model adaptation, using a matched 400M encoder-decoder model.

items.title: HerHealthGPT: An Evidence-Grounded Conversational AI System for Women's Reproductive Health Copy title
items.summary: HerHealthGPT is introduced as an evidence-grounded conversational AI system designed for women's reproductive health. It aims to improve AI responses to health queries by seeking essential context and grounding guidance in verifiable evidence.

items.title: Schema-Free Text-to-SQL: Learning Enterprise Database Structure from Query Logs
items.summary: This paper introduces a method for Text-to-SQL systems to learn enterprise database structures from query logs, improving performance in real-world deployments where complete schema documentation is often absent. It addresses the gap between academic benchmarks and practical application of Text-to-SQL.

items.title: What Makes a Question Curious? Measuring Model Curiosity in Human-LLM Interactions
items.summary: This study investigates and proposes a method for measuring 'model curiosity' in human-LLM interactions, focusing on the LLM's ability to ask insightful questions that identify knowledge gaps or assumptions. It aims to understand and improve LLMs' interactive questioning capabilities.

items.title: Detection of false positives by human reviewers depends on the face recognition algorithm and its security configuration
items.summary: This research investigates how the detection of false positives by human reviewers in face recognition systems is influenced by the specific algorithm used and its security configuration. It highlights challenges in human oversight of highly accurate FR systems.

items.title: Saga: an in silico ontology for a multimodal patient world model
items.summary: This paper introduces Saga, an in silico ontology designed for a multimodal patient world model, enabling the simulation of individual disease courses. It aims to connect patient history with future events for longitudinal prediction and multimodal representations.

items.title: GMoE-FTI: A Universal Facial Template Inversion Method Adopting Genuine Mixture-of-Experts Mechanism
items.summary: This paper proposes GMoE-FTI, a universal facial template inversion method that uses a Mixture-of-Experts mechanism to reconstruct faces from facial templates. It addresses privacy concerns related to face recognition systems storing templates instead of raw images.

items.title: Aerial-R1: Reinforcing Aerial Reasoning and Segmentation in MLLMs
items.summary: This paper introduces Aerial-R1, a method aimed at reinforcing aerial reasoning and segmentation capabilities in Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs). It seeks to mitigate hallucination issues that MLLMs exhibit when processing aerial domain imagery.

items.title: DRA-SAM: Disagreement-Driven Referential Active SAM for Low-Altitude Drone Referring Segmentation
items.summary: This paper proposes DRA-SAM, a disagreement-driven referential active learning method based on the Segment Anything Model (SAM), designed for improved referring segmentation in low-altitude drone imagery. It addresses challenges in distinguishing small, similar instances.

items.title: MOSAIC: Towards a Universal Latent Space for Computational Pathology Foundation Models
items.summary: This research introduces MOSAIC, a framework exploring the creation of a universal latent space for Computational Pathology Foundation Models. It investigates whether these diverse models learn fundamentally shared underlying feature representations.

items.title: MARC: Mechanism-Aware Reflective Correction for Articulated Object Code Generation
items.summary: This paper introduces MARC, a Mechanism-Aware Reflective Correction method for articulated object code generation, ensuring that generated objects can execute their intended motions. It addresses challenges in creating functional complex mechanisms from images and text.

items.title: Oddin: Latent Visual Reasoning in Unified Multimodal Models via Self-Distillation from Image Generation
items.summary: This paper presents Oddin, a method for latent visual reasoning in Unified Multimodal Models (ULMMs) through self-distillation from image generation. It aims to enable efficient visual reasoning without explicit intermediate image generation.

items.title: ProtoEEG: Structured Prototype Alignment for EEG Visual Decoding
items.summary: This paper introduces ProtoEEG, a method using structured prototype alignment for EEG visual decoding, which aims to overcome the challenges of noisy and variable scalp recordings. It focuses on improving the alignment of EEG trials with image embeddings.

items.title: PhaseBreak: Proactive Temporal Protection against Unauthorized Image-to-Video Animation
items.summary: This paper introduces PhaseBreak, a method for proactive visual protection against unauthorized Image-to-Video animation, allowing image owners to apply perturbations to prevent their images from being used for motion synthesis without consent.

items.title: VLMProbe: An Open-source Library for VLM Probing and Interpretation
items.summary: This paper presents VLMProbe, an open-source library designed for probing and interpreting Vision-Language Models (VLMs) by integrating various analysis techniques. It helps researchers understand how VLMs process and use visual information internally.

items.title: AGQ: Action-Guided Ultra-Low-Bit Quantization for Vision-Language-Action Models
items.summary: This paper introduces AGQ (Action-Guided Ultra-Low-Bit Quantization), a method for optimizing Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models. It aims to reduce their memory footprint for deployment on resource-constrained onboard platforms, while preserving task performance.

items.title: Diagnosing and Mitigating Evidence Misgrounding in Multimodal Knowledge Editing
items.summary: This paper investigates evidence misgrounding in Multimodal Knowledge Editing for MLLMs, proposing methods to diagnose and mitigate instances where models produce correct answers but rely on incorrect visual evidence.

items.title: Evaluating Visual Language Models on Visual Grounding for Visually Impaired People
items.summary: This research evaluates the visual grounding capabilities of Visual Language Models (VLMs) in the context of visual question answering (VQA), specifically assessing their potential utility for visually impaired people.

items.title: The Paired Thermal Channel Is Two Orthogonal Axes: A Controlled Attribution Study of Calibration Cost and Detection Gain in Infrared Person Detection
items.summary: This study attributes the detection gain in infrared person detection to the calibrated thermal channel, demonstrating that calibrated ΔT outperforms scale-matched grayscale pseudo-ΔT for improved performance.

items.title: Ampe-DB: A Dataset for Human Activity and Interaction Analysis Using the Ghanaian Game Ampe
items.summary: Ampe-DB is introduced as a new multimodal dataset for human activity and interaction analysis, based on the traditional Ghanaian game Ampe to represent culturally situated movements.

items.title: Learning Pathology-Sensitive Representations for Unsupervised Retinal OCT Anomaly Detection
items.summary: This research focuses on learning pathology-sensitive representations for unsupervised anomaly detection in retinal optical coherence tomography (OCT), enhancing the ability to find rare abnormalities.

items.title: Support-guided OOD Removal with Diffusion
items.summary: This study explores support-guided out-of-distribution (OOD) removal using diffusion models to recover clean signals from observations corrupted by localized, structured perturbations.

items.title: Of Chains and Gains: What Reinforcement Learning changes on Reasoning-based Image Quality Assessment
items.summary: This research examines how Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards (RLVR) influences reasoning-based Image Quality Assessment (IQA) in Vision-Language Models (VLMs), analyzing improvements from Chain-of-Thought reasoning.

items.title: The Locality Trade-off in Masked Patch Self-Distillation
items.summary: This paper investigates the locality trade-off in masked patch self-distillation, a key component of vision foundation models like DINOv2 and DINOv3, revealing its implications for local visual information.

items.title: Automated identification of ivory carvings using machine learning: A proof-of-concept approach to detecting the illegal wildlife trade
items.summary: A proof-of-concept approach demonstrates automated identification of ivory carvings using machine learning, aiming to detect and combat the illegal wildlife trade in online marketplaces.

items.title: Image Clustering with Vision-Language Model Embeddings
items.summary: This research evaluates the suitability of Vision-Language Model embeddings for image clustering, comparing various representation pipelines, image domains, and partitioning algorithms across multiple benchmarks.

items.title: Compression of Vision Foundation Models for Retinal OCT via Growing-Neural-Gas Codebooks and Graph-Guided Masked Image Modeling
items.summary: This paper presents a topology-aware discretization framework for compressing vision foundation models for retinal OCT via Growing-Neural-Gas codebooks and graph-guided masked image modeling, enabling point-of-care deployment.

items.title: Real Time Motion Detection in Video Inspired by Photonic Time Stretch
items.summary: This research proposes a new real-time motion detection method for video, inspired by photonic time stretch, to address challenges faced by traditional computer vision approaches.

items.title: How Robust Are CNNs and Vision Transformers for Alzheimer's MRI Classification Across Datasets?
items.summary: This paper evaluates the robustness of CNNs and Vision Transformers for classifying Alzheimer's disease stages from MRI scans across different datasets. It assesses their performance and limitations in a medical application context.

items.title: Dynamic Query as Budgeting for Tiny Object Detection
items.summary: This research proposes a method to clarify the effects of dynamic query mechanisms in DETR-based tiny object detectors. It aims to improve understanding and design of query strategies for handling density imbalance.

items.title: Semantic-First MixGRPO: Reliable Emotional Image Generation via Temporal Decoupling
items.summary: This paper introduces Semantic-First MixGRPO, a new method for reliable emotional image generation. It uses temporal decoupling to modify visual affect without altering objects, layout, or relations specified in the prompt.

items.title: MarineLife-16K: An Attribute-Rich Video-Text Dataset for Motion-Aware Marine Video Understanding
items.summary: This paper introduces MarineLife-16K, a new attribute-rich video-text dataset for motion-aware marine video understanding. It aims to address limitations in existing datasets by providing more extensive data, detailed text descriptions, and visual attributes.

items.title: Energy Efficient Lung Tumor Segmentation with a modified CBAM ENet Skip Model
items.summary: This research proposes a modified CBAM ENet Skip Model for energy-efficient lung tumor segmentation. It aims to achieve high accuracy while reducing computational demands for early detection and treatment planning.

items.title: Can One Hear Geometry? Gauge-Invariant Spectral Descriptors for Text-to-B-rep Retrieval
items.summary: This paper explores the use of gauge-invariant spectral descriptors for text-to-3D solid retrieval, addressing challenges in aligning natural language with precise geometry. It aims to improve retrieval despite variations in object pose, scale, and recording conventions.

items.title: Explicit Frictional Contact Modeling in Neural Garment Simulation
items.summary: This research focuses on explicitly modeling frictional contact within neural garment simulation using graph neural networks. It aims to improve the realism and control of garment behavior with settable friction coefficients.

items.title: FreqPKC: Frequency-Aware PeakConv for Radar Semantic Segmentation
items.summary: This paper introduces FreqPKC (Frequency-Aware PeakConv), a new neural operator for radar semantic segmentation in autonomous driving. It enhances existing methods like PeakConv by incorporating frequency awareness for robustness in adverse conditions.

items.title: Component Pooling Trained Across Orientations for Few-Shot Remote Sensing Scene Classification
items.summary: This paper proposes a component pooling method trained across orientations for few-shot remote sensing scene classification. It improves upon global average pooling by better summarizing feature maps for novel scene categories.

items.title: Promise and Limits of Cross-Architecture Knowledge Distillation for Lightweight Medical Vision Transformers (LiteMed-ViT)
items.summary: This research investigates the effectiveness and limitations of cross-architecture knowledge distillation for creating lightweight medical Vision Transformers (LiteMed-ViT). It aims to enable efficient medical image analysis on edge devices.

items.title: Patch-Derived or Register Tokens? Comparing Variable-Length Image Tokenizers
items.summary: This paper compares different variable-length image tokenization strategies, specifically patch-derived versus register tokens. It evaluates their efficiency in converting pixels into compact latent sequences for generative modeling.

items.title: Cross-Scale Sparse Attention for Referring Segmentation in Remote Sensing
items.summary: This paper introduces cross-scale sparse attention for referring segmentation in high-resolution remote sensing imagery. This method aims to accurately segment regions described by natural language, improving upon existing sequential approaches.

items.title: End-to-end prostate lesion segmentation and detection from undersampled diffusion-weighted MRI
items.summary: This paper presents an end-to-end network for prostate lesion segmentation and detection directly from undersampled diffusion-weighted MRI data. It leverages complex multicoil DWI data to improve diagnostic accuracy.

items.title: GeoLift: Grounding Video Spatial Reasoning in Explicit 3D Maps
items.summary: This paper introduces GeoLift, a method to improve video spatial reasoning in multimodal large language models by grounding them in explicit 3D maps. It addresses the challenge of integrating observations across viewpoints for complex spatial tasks.

items.title: Interpretable Collision Avoidance and Feasibility Guarantees through an Uncertainty Aware Pipeline
items.summary: This research proposes an uncertainty-aware pipeline to provide interpretable collision avoidance and feasibility guarantees for autonomous vehicles. It addresses the challenge of simultaneously ensuring safety and real-time operation in dynamic environments.

items.title: Causal-based approaches to explain and learn from self-extension - A review
items.summary: This paper presents a review of causal-based approaches used to explain and learn from self-extension in autonomous robotics. It covers advancements in deep learning and automated planning for enhancing robot capabilities.

items.title: Tiny Recursive Policy: Recursive Latent Refinement for Visuomotor Control
items.summary: This paper introduces Tiny Recursive Policy (TRP), a method for robotic manipulation that uses recursive latent refinement for visuomotor control. It aims to maintain persistent latent context throughout execution, improving upon fixed observation windows.

items.title: Active Reachability Learning for Humanoid Recoverability Monitoring
items.summary: This research focuses on active reachability learning to monitor the recoverability of humanoid robots, particularly to anticipate unrecoverable falls. The goal is to synthesize reliable runtime monitors for triggering timely fallback policies.

items.title: MDPO: Multi-constraint Dexterous Policy Optimization with Reinforcement Learning
items.summary: MDPO is a constrained reinforcement learning method for multi-constraint dexterous policy optimization. It enables high-dimensional control policies to accomplish complex contact-rich manipulation tasks while satisfying safety requirements.

items.title: Learning Dexterous Manipulation: Hands, Simulators, Training, and Evaluation
items.summary: This survey reviews 113 learning-based methods for dexterous manipulation, detailing the robotic hands, simulators, and training approaches used in the field. It highlights the convergence on reinforcement learning with privileged information as a common strategy.

items.title: EXE: Egocentric Cross-Embodiment Pretraining via Factorized Latent Actions for VLA Models
items.summary: EXE proposes an egocentric cross-embodiment pretraining method using factorized latent actions to address the data scarcity bottleneck for Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models. It leverages human manipulation videos to improve VLA model capabilities for robotics.

items.title: Quantum Closed Loop Inverse Kinematics Through Hilbert-Space Encoding of Robot Kinematics
items.summary: This paper introduces a structure-preserving quantum representation of rigid-body transformations and serial-manipulator kinematics. It enables closed-loop inverse kinematics for robotics through Hilbert-space encoding, integrating quantum computing into robotics.

items.title: POD-RoPE: Rotary Position Encoding over Physical Observation Distributions for Embodied AI
items.summary: POD-RoPE (Physical Observation Distribution RoPE) is a novel rotary position encoding method for embodied AI, creating positional representations that capture physical geometry and observational extent. It represents token observation footprints as distributions over camera centers.

items.title: RoboReason: Boosting Robotics-Relevant VLM Reasoning Through Scalable Data Generation
items.summary: RoboReason proposes a method to boost robotics-relevant reasoning in Vision-Language Models (VLMs) through scalable data generation. This approach aims to overcome the difficulties and expense of real-world evaluation for downstream robotics tasks.

items.title: On Distributed Sensing and Adversarial Localization of Narrowband Acoustic Sources for Offshore Data Center Monitoring
items.summary: This report investigates a distributed acoustic surveillance framework for localizing and tracking narrowband adversarial sound sources that could threaten offshore data centers.

items.title: A big case study of propensity entanglement
items.summary: A new research paper presents a case study on "propensity entanglement," investigating how propensities generalize out-of-distribution and predicting spillover effects across non-targeted traits.

items.title: Request for Immediate Release of Yang–Mills AI Output
items.summary: The article presents a request for the immediate public release of output generated by an AI system applied to the complex Yang–Mills problem in theoretical physics.

items.title: AI Crisis in Math: Navier-Stokes, Riemann Hypothesis and Complexity Theory [video]
items.summary: This video explores the potential "crisis" in mathematics, discussing how AI might impact or interact with foundational problems like the Navier-Stokes equations, the Riemann Hypothesis, and complexity theory.

items.title: Best AI Tools for Automating Repetitive SEO Tasks
items.summary: The article discusses the best AI tools available for automating repetitive tasks in Search Engine Optimization (SEO).

items.title: Towards an Architecture-Agnostic Definition of "Attention"
items.summary: The post proposes a discussion to develop an architecture-agnostic definition of "Attention" in AI models, exploring fundamental concepts beyond current implementations.

items.title: AI Models Can Provably Hide Arbitrary Capabilities
items.summary: Research indicates that AI models possess the provable capability to hide arbitrary functions or capabilities within their structures.

items.title: US political candidates tailor messages for AI models used by voters
items.summary: US political candidates are tailoring their campaign messages to be effectively processed and understood by AI models that voters might use.

items.title: How to do SEO in 2026: AI Strategies for Better Website Visibility
items.summary: The article provides strategies for optimizing Search Engine Optimization (SEO) in 2026 by leveraging artificial intelligence to improve website visibility.

items.title: Greptile takes bug detection beyond code review with GPT-6 Astra
items.summary: Greptile is utilizing AI models like GPT-6 Astra, Daybreak, and Codex to advance bug detection, strengthen security, and streamline user workflows beyond traditional code review.

items.title: Semantic Labels Guide Terrain-Specific Humanoid Behavior in Simulation - Bioengineer.org
items.summary: New research explores how semantic labels can be used to guide terrain-specific behaviors in humanoid robots within simulated environments, advancing embodied AI.

items.title: Anthropic opens its books for Wall Street, showing record revenue and mounting obligations
items.summary: Anthropic is the first major AI lab to file an S-1 with the SEC, planning to list on the Nasdaq under the ticker "ANT." The numbers are strong, with $11.6 billion in quarterly revenue, a first-ever operating profit, and existing customers spending nine times more year over year. But the company also carries roughly $800 billion in long-term compute commitments. The article Anthropic opens its books for Wall Street, showing record revenue and mounting obligations appeared first on The Decoder .

items.title: Small Groups of Correlated Researchers
items.summary: Summary: The actions taken this decade may be exceptionally important for the future of civilization, but we should be unusually hesitant to proclaim that any course of action is “best.” Still, we should think carefully about what we should do. This post was written as part of an introduction to a new reading group I’m starting called “Doing Good in the Age of AGI.” If you want to follow along, the full curriculum can be found here . Uncertain in the best of times Do you think freezing rent prices would be good for the economic middle class? How confident are you? You might have an answer that you like, but you’re probably not that confident in it. Perhaps you haven’t formally studied economics, but maybe you’ve had some passing interest in the topic. Ever since Mamdani’s mayoral campaign became a talking point across the country, or since his rent freeze passed in June of 2026, discussion of this economic policy has shifted back into the public spotlight. Maybe you’ve tried to read the arguments on both sides, and you’ve noticed that there’s a lot to read. As it turns out, people are opinionated enough that 82% of renters and homebuyers believe there should be caps on rent increases , but a survey of the top economists shows that only 2% [1] think that rent caps would make the middle class substantially better off over the course of a decade (with some of the disagreement coming from whether or not a benefit would be “substantial”) . And within this gap between public sentiment and expert opinion, there is so much discourse and research . The American Economics Association has 23,000 members, about half of which are academics , and a single meta-analysis on rent control reviews over 200 papers . A lot of thinking has gone into finding the truth about this specific question. You might believe that this puts you in a good position to make claims about the effects of rent control. But even if you think expert consensus is pretty unified and easy to defer to, you might fail to explain why, exactly, the occasional dissenter may be wrong or misleading. It’s reasonable for a layperson to feel somewhat uncertain about the efficacy of rent controls, but they can still look toward the thousands of hours of collective thought that have gone into studying this topic to get some answer. The same is also roughly true for the field of climate science, which published over 15,000 peer-reviewed studies in 2025 , and political science, which has thousands of full-time researchers . I bring up rent control because it’s small and specific, has a pretty clear expert consensus, a wide body of evidence to refer to, and yet still remains a large source of public disagreement and uncertainty. Now, imagine trying to answer a question that has none of those qualities. A question like, “How can we do the most good?” No question may be more important than, “What is the most important problem for us to work on?” Despite this, it receives much less attention globally than the content of an introductory economics class. In 2025, GiveWell had about 40 full-time employees trying to answer the question, “What is the most cost-effective way to save a life, given the best evidence we have?” That same year, Animal Charity Evaluators had about 12 FTEs trying to figure out which animal welfare strategies will actually help animals, and as of October 2026, Coefficient Giving has 55 people on their Global Catastrophic Risks team (although not all of them are directly doing prioritization work). In 2025, Rethink Priorities estimated that there were only about 20 total FTEs in the world trying to determine the most important cause to work on, and only 4 FTEs trying to compare the cost-effectiveness of interventions across different causes . [2] And only a fraction of these employees are trying to answer this question by considering the possibility of truly transformative AI. If you look ahead at the curriculum’s future weeks, you may notice that Forethought (an organization with close to 16 FTEs) has contributed about 9 of our required readings and 3 of our additional recommendations. [3] Aside from the number of researchers being small, they’re also highly correlated in the sense that many of them hold similar assumptions, many of which could turn out to be false. In the entire curriculum, there are only four readings I’m not confident are written by effective altruists. [4] Their authors are Eliezer Yudkowsky (the primary founder of the rationalist movement), Jason Hausenloy (who I feel less confident about being an EA because he works at CAIS), the Forecasting Research Institute (which receives funding from Coefficient Giving), and something called “The Greater Good Magazine.” A relatively small cultural lineage is producing the vast majority of our understanding about this topic. There’s a strong, mathematical reason to be deathly afraid of these correlations, and it has to do with our ability to get rid of the Optimizer’s Curse . The curse works something like this: imagine you’re trying to figure out which cause area (out of 30 or so) is the most important. When you make an impact evaluation for each cause, your estimate will include both the size of a cause’s true impact and the size of any mistakes you made in your assessment. As a result, when you try to choose the most important cause area, you’ll probably choose something that you’ve significantly overestimated the importance of by making a mistake. Graph showing the Optimizer’s Curse. We only see our estimation of the impact, rather than the actual impact, which causes us to ignore the best cause in favor of a cause whose impact we overestimated. And, when you’re extra uncertain about something (such as what the future will look like, or what threat has the highest chance of causing extinction), the size of the curse is amplified . [5] If we have a diverse pool of researchers evaluating causes independently, this can significantly reduce how much we overestimate the top cause. But if the researchers are correlated and share the same mistakes, no number of separate researchers will be able to get rid of the curse completely. Graph: Using Titotal’s Optimizer’s Curse model for existential risks , I simulated 10,000 instances of 500 different researchers evaluating the danger of different causes, aggregating their results, and estimating the impact of working on the top one. Different r values correspond to different levels of correlated mistakes. When their mistakes are completely uncorrelated (r = 0), aggregating research results leads to no Optimizer’s Curse most of the time, while researchers who share many of the same mistakes (high r value) significantly overestimate the size of the top threat most of the time. When writing this curriculum, I did my best to include readings from a good number of perspectives, but in practice, so few people are taking time to think seriously about what transformative AI could do to the future and how we can best prepare for it. If we’re going to get AGI or ASI by 2040, then most of our best guesses for how to make the future good are currently coming from small groups of highly correlated researchers. This should make us terrified. Moving Forward There’s a lot of work to be done and a lot of wrong ways to do it, but we still may have good reasons to be optimistic about our room for progress. Our understanding of transformative AI cause prioritization is limited enough that someone smart can say valuable things within a few months of thinking about these problems. It’s small enough that I felt comfortable making this reading group six weeks long, instead of eight. If you set aside the time to do some research, talk to some experts, and perhaps do a “ minimal trust investigation ”, you can make helpful critiques that sharpen our models of the world. Even if your arguments miss important context or internal research , the broader community still benefits from the information you share. At the end of the day, Forethought is just a bunch of smart people who have taken time to think about highly neglected fields. It wouldn’t take a newcomer especially long to make similarly helpful contributions. [6] But while novel work can help, there are wrong ways to adjust for a lack of differing perspectives. We reduce the overestimations caused by Optimizer’s Curse by correcting our mistaken beliefs, and not every challenge is a correction. Taking on diverse views simply for the sake of getting different answers does not necessarily bring us closer to the truth, the same way that the best forecasters will not make better predictions by averaging their predictions with worse predictions. If you disagree with someone about something, figure out what evidence has led them to believe something different than you, and see if you can reconcile this gap. But even though the groups thinking seriously about these problems are pretty small, I feel hopeful about the EA community’s ability to make some good judgments. They respond well to criticism , challenge each other’s assumptions, and are keen to build more accurate models of the world . The EA community also disproportionately produces superforecasters and supports tons of forecasting research because they earnestly try to improve at this. When I was writing this post, I tried to make a list of mistakes that the AI safety community had historically made, that should have been obvious to avoid. Most examples [7] I found were contested, hard to predict, and were quickly pivoted away from when shown to be false. For the most part, our models of the future are limited because of a lack of time and resources, not because of a lack of care on behalf of the people making them. [8] At the end of the day, though, our understanding of the future is limited. If we try to prepare for any specific vision of it, we will certainly make mistakes, and there’s a large chance our work could be trivial or net-negative. Despite this, I think that trying our best to improve the lives of the many future generations of humans, animals, and other sentient creatures yet to come is one of the most important things we can do. ^ The single economist in the survey who thinks the proposed rent control would be substantially positive has 18,000 citations , is the Haas Distinguished Chair in Economic Disparities at UC Berkeley, and primarily studies the impact of tax and transfer programs on low-income families. She rates her confidence a 5/10. On these credentials and evidence alone, it’s not completely obvious how this evidence should be weighed. ^ Of course, full-time employees aren’t the only people who make meaningful contributions to this effort. Many people engaged in EA think about cause prioritization in their free time and make valuable contributions on the EA Forum and LessWrong. Many people working in EA causes do some amount of cause prioritization as only part of their job. A notable number of people not directly engaged with EA (especially economists) spend some amount of time thinking and writing about it. And a large amount of successful prioritization work relies on the work of economists, biologists, philosophers, and other researchers who lay the groundwork for careful study. Still, I think FTEs are a helpful metric for comparing field sizes. ^ Numbers may differ based on the version of the curriculum you see ^ Or at least, people I would call effective altruists. People are weird about how they use this term. ^ I’ve probably spent ~20 hours thinking about and drafting a response post to Titotal’s series on The Optimizer’s Curse, and I feel about 90% confident that it’s not a good reason in itself to lower your p(doom) more than 2 OOMs, but I keep putting off writing this post because other things seem more important. If you want to hear my thoughts about this, message me. ^ Alternatively, if you think you already have a lot of helpful inside views and arguments that are underrated in the community, you should write them up! ^ My original passage on this topic, trying to make the strongest (true) version of this case, read: “While the early AI safety community had remarkably good foresight by most reasonable accounts, and there was reasonable disagreement about most claims, some of their common assumptions for modeling AI development ended up being false. I’m not an expert on pre-GPT AI safety discourse, but a list of a few mistakes that captured the AI safety community’s focus before recent years: Early MIRI’s research directions were largely based on Yudkowsky’s belief that superintelligent AI could be hand-built in someone’s basement, without the need for large infrastructure and compute. This also led them to believe that the leading AI project would be small and secretive, with no public insight into what was happening whatsoever. Nick Bostrom spent a lot of time exploring Manhattan Project-style construction, though. The early AI box debates centered around the idea that AIs would not be given economic integration and access to the internet by default; rather, they would need to talk their way into getting this (which they would be able to do). A large portion of the safety community focused on theorizing about how intelligence worked, which they believed would ultimately be required to build more powerful AIs. AI researchers using deep learning ultimately overturned this paradigm, gradually teaching the safety researchers a bitter lesson . These mistakes were, by no means, devastating, but they help illustrate how a limited intellectual lineage might lead to misallocated efforts. Still, I’m sympathetic to the claim that it made sense to approach questions from these lenses at the time, and the community quickly pivoted to better things when they were shown to be wrong.” ^ You might also think we’re clueless about what’s good, anyway, because we have no idea about what the ripple effects of our actions on the very far future will be. This is frustrating, but there’s room for a small comfort: the possibility of AGI-induced lock-in (as the reading group will cover in Week 2) could mean that we’re the least clueless we’ve ever been! items.title: WebAnything: From the Wild Web to Scalable Agent Environments
items.summary: This paper introduces WebAnything, a system designed to create diverse, executable, and resettable website environments for the reproducible training and evaluation of web agents. It aims to overcome limitations of existing methods that are either engineering-intensive or diverge from real websites.

items.title: What Does an Ontology Catch? Curated, LLM-Generated and Data-Derived Ontologies as Checkers of LLM Agents over Knowledge Graphs
items.summary: This research investigates the effectiveness of ontologies, whether curated, LLM-generated, or data-derived, when used as checkers for LLM agents operating over knowledge graphs. It questions the reliability of such formal schemas in identifying errors or falsely flagging correct answers from agents.

items.title: Measuring Where Intent Gets Lost in Agentic Smart Contract Synthesis
items.summary: This research focuses on measuring where the original intent gets lost when AI agents synthesize smart contracts from natural language descriptions. It highlights the critical issue of ensuring functional code also matches the user's request, especially for immutable Web3 applications.

items.title: Detecting Covert Collusion between AI Agents through Partner-Outsider Positive Listening
items.summary: This research proposes a behavioral test, called Partner-Outsider Positive Listening, to detect covert collusion between AI agents that use secret conventions for coordination. The method identifies collusion by observing agents' reactions to the precise wording of messages, indicating shared understanding.

items.title: FilingLoop: Evaluating and Evolving LLM Agents for Corporate Disclosure Review and Revision
items.summary: This paper introduces FilingLoop, a system designed for evaluating and evolving LLM agents tasked with reviewing and revising corporate disclosures from repositories like SEC EDGAR. It addresses the challenges of discovering deficiencies, acquiring facts, and verifying requests in complex financial documents.

items.title: VerifiedLab: Harnessing Knowns for Unknowns
items.summary: This paper introduces VerifiedLab, addressing the need for new conventions to preserve knowledge as research agents are increasingly deployed for laboratory experiments. It focuses on how to manage and structure knowledge in agent-driven scientific discovery processes.

items.title: GARDEN: Generalist Autonomous Reward Design Through Evidence Navigation for Cooperative Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
items.summary: This research introduces GARDEN (Generalist Autonomous Reward Design Through Evidence Navigation), a method for autonomously designing reward functions for cooperative multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL). GARDEN aims to provide more effective guidance for agent learning beyond simple task success, enabling better coordinated behaviors.

items.title: PromptSense: Sentiment-Aware Mental Health Chatbot with Dynamic Prompting
items.summary: This paper proposes PromptSense, a novel framework for mental health chatbots that integrates sentiment and depression analysis with dynamic prompting to enhance empathy, contextual awareness, and safety. The system aims to address limitations in current LLM-based mental health conversational agents.

items.title: FACTS-MAS: A Multi-Agent Architecture for Adaptive Forecasting from Heterogeneous Evidence
items.summary: FACTS-MAS introduces a domain-agnostic multi-agent architecture for adaptive forecasting that integrates heterogeneous evidence by decomposing it into specialized channels. The framework aims to improve real-world forecasting by adapting to varying predictive values across different contexts.

items.title: Investor's Last Exam: Can AI Agents Do Equity Investment Without Seeing the Future?
items.summary: This research explores whether AI agents can effectively perform equity investment tasks by forming forecasts and investment judgments based on real-time evidence, assessing their full research process.

items.title: SCOPE: Selective Critical-Step On-Policy Self-Distillation for Agentic Reinforcement Learning
items.summary: This paper introduces SCOPE, a method for selective critical-step on-policy self-distillation to improve the learning process for long-horizon LLM agents in reinforcement learning.

items.title: Masked Erosion: How Acceptance Gates Lose Redundant Safeguards in Self-Improving Agents
items.summary: This research investigates how "acceptance gates" in self-improving LLM agents can inadvertently lead to the loss of redundant safeguards when agents edit their own prompts and rules.

items.title: Agent Transfer Protocol: Server-Mediated Agent-to-Agent Communication Architecture for the Agentic Web
items.summary: This paper proposes an "Agent Transfer Protocol," a server-mediated communication architecture designed to enable continuous and stable collaboration among AI agents from different organizations on the Agentic Web.

items.title: Governance-Aware Federated Learning for Multi-Agent AI Systems: A Policy-Driven Framework for Trustworthy Collaborative AI
items.summary: This paper proposes Governance-Aware Federated Learning (GAFL), a policy-driven framework for multi-agent AI systems to enable trustworthy collaborative AI with enhanced runtime governance, fairness, and auditability.

items.title: Predict the Reward, Not the World: World Reward Models for ML Agents
items.summary: This research introduces "World Reward Models" to improve search-based machine learning agents by allowing them to predict rewards directly, thus saving computation time from executing discarded candidate programs.
